review.summary: The zone's skeleton reads as Victory Monument. The named roads with medians, the roundabout with its obelisk, the skywalk ring, the BTS curving round the east side, and the canal with its bridge are all recognisable, and the shophouse prefabs are the most authentic Thai thing in the game. Realism and play break down in the fill between the roads. About two-thirds of block land (65,703 of 98,896 cells) is a grid of about 45 near-identical slabs laid out by the packer, 10 of them full "hospitals", standing on speckled lawns. The shophouse blocks are a lattice of 1-2-unit rows with through-sois everywhere and no dead ends. The main roads and the four corners of the monument have no shop fronts: shop fronts can only face south, and the land where they could face a road went to walled compounds. Most fixes are data (splitting blocks in victory.cfg, new block keys, a trades table) plus two focused rewrites (_big_block packing and _shophouse_block rows/sois). They can ship together as one GEN 10 bump, and the same work builds the agreed next step (a temple refugee camp) and a readable risk gradient from the camp out to the hospitals.
strengths: The central hub is right and memorable: the roundabout with the obelisk and soldier statues, a garden ring, the raised skywalk ring, and the BTS deck sweeping round the east side down to a station on Phaya Thai (01_monument, 16_wide, 02_phahon_bts; city_gen.gd:199-211, 248-290).

The shophouse prefabs are genuinely Thai: rolling-shutter fronts, stairs in the middle of the plot, a back kitchen with a water jar (โอ่ง) and squat toilet, bedrooms upstairs, shared party walls, pavements dressed per trade (FRONTS), motorbikes parked nose-in, and spirit houses (09_shophouse_sw, 10_shophouse_e, 17-19; data/prefabs/home.txt; city_gen.gd:797-826, 1044-1069, 1169-1202).

The pipeline is table-driven, deterministic and save-aware: a whole zone is a 58-line cfg, prefabs are text files, the late passes (_shop_fronts, _landmarks, _zone_exits) use their own RNG so saves stay valid, and tests/test_city.gd guards the result with a fingerprint.

Street texture is strong: red-and-white kerbs, a power pole every 6 cells with sagging wires and lamps, a Thai vehicle mix (songthaews, buses in three liveries, tuk-tuks, minivans), and an aftermath story (pile-ups at junctions, an army checkpoint, dropped luggage) (02, 12_ratchawithi, 15_ratchaprarop; city_gen.gd:886-923, 995-1163).

BigPlans interiors follow the real Bangkok corridor building: stairs at both ends, a dead lift, a lobby with a Buddha shelf, a generator plant room, pharmacy counters, curtained wards and loot by room type, plus a rooftop helipad on large hospitals (big_plans.gd:54-113, 177-269; building_prop.gd:690-695; 04, 20).

The level-design bones already exist: walled hospital compounds with a gate roughly every 32 cells act as chokepoints (city_gen.gd:720-732), the canal is a barrier crossed by one bridge that you can also swim to escape, shophouse roofs join along a row (world.gd:896-899), vehicles can be climbed, and the M map reveals as you explore.

findings.title: Big-building compounds are a repeated slab grid: about 45 slabs, 10 of them hospitals
findings.observation: FACT: 66% of block land (65,703 of 98,896 cells) is compound use. _big_block fills rows left to right and top to bottom from the inner top-left corner, with 6-12 cell gaps, and cycles the kinds in BLOCK_USES (kinds[k % size]). Only the mall stops after one building. Counted from 00_zone_map: the NW military block holds 4x4 = 16 slabs (8 hospitals, all signed "โรงพยาบาลทหาร", 4 flats, 4 offices). The NE block holds about 20 (10 offices, 10 flats) and the W hospital block holds 3 (2 hospitals). Every hospital is the same complete building (lobby, pharmacy, wards). Leftover land ends up on the right and bottom of each block, which is exactly beside Phahon Yothin and Ratchawithi. In 04_mil_hospital and 06_office the compounds read as a business park.
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:634-640 (BLOCK_USES), 651-682 (packer; kinds[k % kinds.size()] at 661; mall break 675-677), 698-703 (signs); big_plans.gd:14-20; 00_zone_map.png (NW and NE quadrants); 04_mil_hospital.png; 06_office.png
findings.why: A real Bangkok hospital campus has one dominant main building, distinct annexes, a parking structure and staff flats, with shophouses pressed against it. Ten identical hospitals undo "the hospital is the dangerous place worth a planned trip" (ROADMAP: สิ่งที่ต้องทำด้วยกัน; difficulty labels บ้านแถว < ห้าง/ตลาด < โรงพยาบาล). They also flood the zone with medicine and make navigation impossible, because every compound block looks the same.
findings.suggestion: (1) Add a per-block "kinds" list in victory.cfg, e.g. {"use":"military_hospital","kinds":["hospital","wards","flats","flats"]}. _big_block uses it when present and stops once the list is placed, with no modulo cycling. (2) Fill from the road-facing (south) edge: start at inner.end.y and move north, so fronts and drop-offs face the road and leftover land becomes a back service yard. (3) Shrink compounds to what they need and hand the freed land to shophouse or condo sub-blocks (L2, L3). For example: the military hospital becomes 1 main hospital, 1 ward block and 2 nurse flats; the W block becomes 1 hospital; NE becomes 3 office towers near the roundabout and 1-2 condos. (4) Add two cheap BigPlans kinds that reuse _corridor: "wards" (ward floors only, no lobby or pharmacy) and "carpark" (open floors of parked cars, fuel to siphon). (5) Give each building its own name through SIGN_NAMES by index (ตึกผู้ป่วยนอก, ตึกอุบัติเหตุ, ตึกพักพยาบาล 2) instead of 8 identical signs.

findings.title: Shophouse blocks are a lattice of 1-2-unit rows with through-sois everywhere
findings.observation: FACT: a cross-soi starts every 12-16 cells and runs the full height of the block, so each row segment is 9-13 cells wide, which fits 1-2 shophouses. Every row gets its own 3-cell soi in front. All sois are exactly 3 wide and all of them run through; there are no dead ends. The only narrower gap is a 7% chance of a 2-cell walkway. Leftover rows (fewer than 13) are dumped at the block's bottom edge as vacant lot, which is the edge where fronts should meet the street (the green strip at the bottom of the SE block in 00_zone_map). 00_zone_map shows the SW and SE blocks as a checkerboard of pairs; 09 and 10 show 2-unit rows with a soi on each side.
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:760-792 (_shophouse_block: cols 762-766, row soi 782, leftover 784-792), 807-810 (7% walkway); world.gd:896-899 (roofs join only along a row); 00_zone_map.png SW/SE; 09_shophouse_sw.png; 10_shophouse_e.png
findings.why: Real Bangkok rows run 6-20 units before a soi. A superblock is entered by a few deep fishbone sois, many of them dead ends, with 1-2 m ตรอก between. For play: roofs join only along a row, so 2-unit rows kill rooftop escape. A lattice means zombies arrive from every side at every corner, and there are no quiet pockets to claim as home, no dead-end traps and no chokepoints to hold.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite _shophouse_block: (a) lay rows from the south (road) edge upward, so leftover space becomes a 1-2 cell back alley or lot at the back. (b) Add one main soi (5 wide; _vehicle already parks on SOI) every 40-70 cells, starting at the road edge and running in. (c) Keep the rows between main sois continuous at 6-10 units. (d) Add a 2-cell ตรอก every ~25 cells that cuts through only 1-3 rows, making dead ends. (e) Draw front-soi widths from [3,3,3,4,5]. (f) Keep today's short comb (a soi every 12-16 cells) only within ~20 cells of a north-south road; in the 3/4 view, that comb is how shop fronts show toward a N-S road. (g) Flood-fill to check every door can reach a road, and open a 2-cell walkway where one can't. Make the spacing a block key ("soi_every": [40,70]) so Pratunam can differ. Do not try north-facing rows: the camera shows only south faces.

findings.title: Main roads and the monument's corners have no shop frontage
findings.observation: FACT: shop fronts can only face south (victory.cfg:37-38; the bottom row of every prefab). Rows are laid from a block's top edge, so a block south of a road shows its roofs and backs to it. The blocks north of both halves of Ratchawithi, north of ถนนโยธี and north of Soi Rang Nam are all walled or lawned compounds. Result: Ratchawithi, Phahon Yothin and Phaya Thai have no fronts facing them. 11_play_zoom (default zoom on ถนนโยธี) shows only roofs, 12 shows walls, and 02 shows lawn on one side and an office's side wall on the other. All four corners of the monument are lawns with trees (16_wide, 01), because _on_circle pushes big buildings away and the freed ground turns to lawn.
findings.evidence: victory.cfg:34-48; city_gen.gd:668-670 (_big_block skips circle), 684-694 (lawn), 774-783 (rows from top), 818-823; 11_play_zoom.png; 12_ratchawithi.png; 02_phahon_bts.png; 16_wide.png; 01_monument.png
findings.why: Bangkok's main roads are continuous walls of shophouse fronts, and the Victory Monument corners are among the busiest pavements in the city: bus stops, skywalk stairs, vendors. From the map the zone looks right, but at play zoom the hub reads as a park.
findings.suggestion: Data first, with no drawing changes: carve a 15-row "shophouses" strip off the south edge of every block that lies north of an east-west road, so its fronts face the road. Examples: {"rect":[0,136,191,15],"use":"shophouses"} with military_hospital shrunk to [0,24,191,112]; [209,136,191,15] with office shrunk to [209,24,191,112]; [60,203,131,15] along ถนนโยธี with the hospital block shrunk to [0,169,191,34]. The strip's cross-sois will dead-end at the compound wall, which is realistic. Also let _wall_round (city_gen.gd:729) put gates where the outside cell is SOI, not only SIDEWALK, so the compounds get back gates. For block edges that sit south of a road, use things that look right from behind: a compound wall, a vacant lot behind a corrugated fence, a petrol-station forecourt, a temple wall. Corners: pave the freed quarter-circles as PLAZA and dress them in a last pass with its own RNG, like _landmarks: vendor-stall clusters, a skywalk stair landing at each corner, a police booth.

findings.title: A drawn zone cannot place a temple or park, and the refugee-camp spawn needs a temple
findings.observation: FACT: _layout_plan sends a block to _big_block if its use is in BLOCK_USES and to _shophouse_block otherwise. _temple_block (walls with 4 gates, temple hall, chedi, sala, trees), _condo_block and _park_block (pond, jogging paths) all exist, and BuildingProp still draws temple, chedi, sala and condo, but only the random _layout_sections calls them (used by the Pratunam placeholder). Victory has no temple and no park. ROADMAP 'ชั่วโมงแรก' makes the next agreed item a refugee camp in a temple that serves as every new player's spawn.
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:214-220 (dispatch), 829-869 (temple/condo/park), 356-361 (only caller); building_prop.gd:42-51, 136-144; ROADMAP.md:378 (ค่ายผู้อพยพ ในวัด = จุดเกิด)
findings.why: Temples are the most common non-shop landmark in any Bangkok soi network. The camp is the "go home" end of the core loop and the safe centre of the risk gradient.
findings.suggestion: In _layout_plan, match b.use: "temple" goes to _temple_block, "park" to _park_block, "condo" to _condo_block. Replace _temple_block's hard-coded offsets (built for a ~30x32 block) with offsets that scale to the block, so a ~40x40 camp temple works with a courtyard for tents. Add nested blocks: place reserved-use blocks first, record their rects, and have _row skip plots that overlap them, the same way it already skips the roundabout (818-823). Authors can then drop a temple inside the SW shophouse block without splitting it into four rects. Placement: a fictional, non-royal community temple deep in the SW block, reached by a wide temple soi off ถนนโยธี, about 60 cells from the current spawn. Also a small public park near Rang Nam/Ratchaprarop; I believe the real area has one (สวนสันติภาพ), but verify on OSM.

findings.title: The risk gradient is flat, and new players spawn in the most exposed spot
findings.observation: FACT: plan spawn [191,176] is on the roundabout carriageway (18 cells from the centre, inside r=28), between the hospital-district compound and the military-hospital compound. The nearest enterable buildings are big ones, whose trapped zombies are let out when a player comes within 900 px. The first shophouses are 55+ cells away (the SW block starts at y=230). My estimate from Buildings.trapped_start: hospitals, offices, flats and malls all land at about 9-14 trapped (cap 14); only markets are lower (2-8). So a hospital is no scarier than an office. Street zombies spawn uniformly 320-840 px around each player, whatever the place.
findings.evidence: victory.cfg:8; city_gen.gd:199-203 (circle ROAD r=28); buildings.gd:37-46; survival.gd:453-475 (uniform spawn), 530-532 (let out within NEAR=900); main.gd:12-13
findings.why: The fun principle is choosing your own risk. That needs a readable gradient: temple camp (safe), then inner sois and homes, then frontage shops, then market and mall, then the hospital and military compound. ROADMAP round 2 plans difficulty labels by place, and the layout has to deliver that ladder.
findings.suggestion: (1) Move plan.spawn to the temple camp (L4). Ship it in the same GEN bump, because _aftermath's pile-up and checkpoint rolls depend on the spawn (city_gen.gd:999, 1142). (2) Add a "danger" key per block in victory.cfg, read through the block lookup that already dresses zombies by block (Items.zombie_place, items.gd:455-466). In _spawn_zombie, accept a candidate cell with probability = danger: temple 0, inner sois 0.5, frontage 1.0, compound grounds 1.4. (3) Scale TRAPPED by kind in buildings.gd:45, e.g. {hospital 1.3, mall 1.1, office 0.8, flats 0.7}; this is not a gen change. (4) With L1 there are only 1-2 hospitals, so they become the planned group trip.

findings.title: Dead space: empty fields, forests and speckled lawns
findings.observation: FACT: (a) Everything north of the canal (y 0-13, about 5,400 cells) is grass apart from the road (03_canal, 00). (b) Leftover compound land becomes 85% grass or tree, with the other 15% of cells left as random SOI paving: the speckle in 00_zone_map and the forests in 05 (south half of the hospital block) and 07 (around the mall). (c) Some patches belong to no block: x0-57 by y218-229 (west end of ถนนโยธี) and x246-273 by y212-221 (north of the market). (d) Every big building gets a 6-row paved driveway band; in 08 the market faces about 20x12 cells of empty paving with one random grass square.
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:180-183 (canal full width), 683-694 (SOI fill plus 85/15 speckle); victory.cfg:17-19, 39-48; 00_zone_map.png; 03_canal.png; 05_hospital_block.png; 07_mall.png; 08_market.png
findings.why: Walking through nothing is exactly the "walk around, bored" complaint. At zoom 4 (about 20x11 m on screen), a 60-cell wood is 15 screens of trees with no loot and no decision.
findings.suggestion: Aim for every cell to belong to a block with a purpose. Data: the north bank becomes a canal-front row (L7); the west patch extends the SW shophouse block; x246-274 by y212-222 becomes a fenced vacant lot or small park. Code: in _big_block, replace the 85/15 speckle with coherent areas: paved car-park bays in front (parked cars lined up in bays), a 2-cell tree line along walls and driveways (a tree every 4-5 cells), plain lawn elsewhere. Add a cheap "lot" use: a vacant lot behind a corrugated fence (สังกะสี) with overgrown grass, a shack and a dead truck. It is realistic Bangkok filler that still gives something to search.

findings.title: The canal is a blank channel: no bank life, one crossing
findings.observation: FACT: canals run the full map width at fixed rows with 2-cell towpaths. The only crossing is the Phahon Yothin bridge. The north bank is an empty field and the south bank is the hospital wall (03_canal). Boats are rolled every 9 cells at 50%. Swimming is an escape zombies cannot follow (ROADMAP A2).
findings.why: The stretch of Khlong Sam Sen at Victory Monument is known for its boat-noodle alley along the bank. That is one of the district's most recognisable spots and a perfect landmark with no brands and no royal site. Canal-side houses and piers are core Bangkok texture. The canal is also the zone's best escape line, yet nothing along it is worth escaping to or from.
findings.suggestion: (1) victory.cfg: add shophouse strips on the north bank, [0,0,193,14] and [207,0,193,14]. Their fronts face south onto the towpath, i.e. onto the water, which fits the south-only rule. (2) Add a block key "signs" that biases the trade roll (city_gen.gd:379-380 picks from the block's list first); the stretch by the bridge then becomes ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือ and other eateries, a boat-noodle alley. (3) Later: a wooden canal-house prefab (1-2 storeys) and a pier prop with a long-tail boat (Phase 5 boats). (4) Add a narrow second crossing (a 3-cell footbridge) about 80 cells from the road bridge, giving a chokepoint and a loop route.

findings.title: The market is four cloned sheds; the malls stand in lawn with their backs to the road
findings.observation: FACT: BLOCK_USES market = ["market"] cycles, so the 28x95 Rang Nam block holds 4 separate identical sheds, each signed "ตลาดสด ซอยรางน้ำ", each facing a paved forecourt (08). Malls stop after one per block. The 25x95 block gets a small 20-21 wide mall at its top and about 60 rows of lawn below it. Mall 1 is pushed off the roundabout and stands in lawn and trees. Its glass doors face south onto its own driveway, while its back door (B, top row) faces Ratchawithi and the BTS (07).
findings.why: A Thai fresh market is one big shed tucked behind shophouses, reached from a soi, with stalls and carts spilling into that soi. A Bangkok mall fronts the main road with a forecourt of vendors. Four clones make none of them a destination.
findings.suggestion: (1) One market shed per block: stop after one, as with the mall, or use L1's "kinds" list. Author the rest of the block as shophouse frontage on Soi Rang Nam with the market in the middle, reached by a soi. (2) In a last pass with its own RNG, drop existing stall and cart props along the soi within about 15 cells of the market's open sides. (3) Keep one mall in the zone and turn the second mall block into condo or shophouses. Pack the mall against the road edge (L1) so its entrance faces the road and the BTS, and dress the forecourt with carts and a bus stop.

findings.title: Main roads lack the everyday furniture that makes Bangkok streets readable
findings.observation: FACT: bus stops exist only round the roundabout (8 of them). There are no motorbike-taxi (วินมอเตอร์ไซค์) stands and no pedestrian footbridges; the skywalk ring is drawn overhead only. Carts and stalls are random scatter (city_gen.gd:939-941, 1039-1041), not clustered at stations, markets or soi mouths. The test_city fingerprint hashes tiles, doors, containers and buildings only, so extra street props added in a last pass do not break saves.
findings.why: These are what make each 50 m of Bangkok road recognisable, and they double as level design. A win stand means predictable rideable motorbikes at soi mouths (it also sets up the planned "วินมอไซค์" zombie). A bus stop with a dead bus is cover and a roof to climb. A footbridge is a mid-scale landmark you can see at zoom 4.
findings.suggestion: Add a final pass with its own RNG, like _landmarks: a bus stop about every 120 cells on each side of every named road, 30% of them with a bus at the kerb (existing bus/busstop props). At each soi mouth on a main road, a win stand (one new small prop: bench, vest rack, sign) plus 3-5 motorbikes (existing _park). A police booth at one roundabout arm. Vendor clusters at the BTS stairs (city_gen.gd:280-290). Footbridges: an Overhead piece like _draw_skywalk, two across Ratchawithi, with stair props at both ends; make them walkable later with the skywalk (Phase 5). None of this changes tiles, doors, containers or buildings, so no GEN bump is needed.

findings.title: The trade mix ignores location, and everyday Thai trades are missing
findings.observation: FACT: 75% of shophouses get a sign picked uniformly from 18, so gold shops plus pawnshops are 1 in 9 shops everywhere, and homes are 25% everywhere. Floors are a random 2-3. The minimart is a flat 10% roll anywhere in a row, so the blue cells in 00_zone_map sit mid-block, sometimes side by side, and none are at corners. There are 12 prefabs, one plan per trade; there is no neighbourhood grocery (โชห่วย), no drinking-water and LPG shop, no laundry.
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:30-32 (SIGNS), 42-50 (SIGN_LOOT), 376-393 (floors 378, sign roll 379-380), 811-815 (store roll); data/prefabs/*.txt; 00_zone_map.png (blue cells)
findings.why: The real mix follows location. Main-road frontage is almost all trades (about a third food) with 3-4 storeys, and a convenience store at soi mouths. Inner sois are mostly 2-storey homes with the odd grocery or eatery. For play: frontage is where you scavenge goods and inner sois are the homes to claim (ROADMAP home claiming). Grocery and water/gas shops feed the water, food and cooking loop; stoves use gas 2-6 times.
findings.suggestion: Move SIGNS into a table, data/trades.cfg, with columns: sign, weight, where (front/inner/canal), loot table. Give rows a shop rate by position: 0.9 if the row faces a road pavement, 0.35 inside. Set floors to 3-4 on frontage and 2 inside. Store chance: 0.5 for the unit at a row end beside a road, 0.03 elsewhere. Add 3 prefabs, each a .txt plus rows in SIGNS, SIGN_LOOT and FRONTS: โชห่วย (shelves of canned food, rice sacks, water packs), ร้านน้ำดื่ม-แก๊ส (LPG cylinders and drinking water), and a laundry.

findings.title: Places have names in the data, but players never see them
findings.observation: FACT: roads are named in victory.cfg and stored on w.roads, but nothing reads the name. city_map.gd draws only the exit labels and player pins, and there are no in-world street or soi signs. Block names reach players only as hospital and market building signs. At the default zoom (11_play_zoom, about 20x11 m) the player sees about three shop fronts and no landmark except the BTS deck.
findings.evidence: victory.cfg:11-20, 39-48; city_gen.gd:190, 698-702; city_map.gd:205-226 (only exits and pins drawn); 11_play_zoom.png
findings.why: Co-op needs words for places ("meet at ซอยราชวิถี 7, by the gold shop"), and quests or the radio can point to them. Getting lost in a samey grid is the other half of "walk around, bored".
findings.suggestion: (1) M map: draw road names along each road rect and block names at block centres. This is pure UI, no gen change. (2) In a last pass with its own RNG: a blue road-name sign at every junction and a numbered soi sign at every soi mouth, numbered the Bangkok way, odd on one side and even on the other ("ซ.พหลโยธิน 3"). Store the number on the soi so the map and quests can use it. (3) Number the buildings inside a compound (ตึก 1-4). (4) Aim for a mid-scale landmark every 60-80 cells: a footbridge (L9), the temple chedi (L4), a rooftop billboard frame, a water tower.

findings.title: Block vocabulary and feedback loop limit zone design speed
findings.observation: FACT: a zone is 8 block rects and 8 road rects. A block can only be shophouses or one of 5 compound uses, with no keys for kinds, trades, danger or frontage. Carving a strip or a temple (L3, L4) means hand-splitting rects. Checking a change means launching the game and opening M (00_zone_map was taken that way). ROADMAP 'แผนที่ใหญ่' says the real limiter is zone design time, and Pratunam is still the _layout_sections placeholder.
findings.why: Every finding above gets cheaper, and zone 2 gets faster, if blocks can say more and a layout can be checked in seconds.
findings.suggestion: (1) Block keys: use (add temple, park, condo, lot, carpark; later school, police, petrol), kinds (an explicit building list), front (auto shophouse strip along road-facing edges), shops (rate), signs or trades, danger, soi_every. (2) Nested blocks: later blocks reserve their rect inside earlier ones. (3) A headless script (e.g. tools/zone_png.gd, run with godot --headless) that builds a zone and writes the M-map image with road and block names and a legend (compound kinds, stores, unassigned grass highlighted). Use it on every cfg edit and as a before/after for GEN bumps. (4) Add the south-facing rule to data/zones/README.txt: "put shop strips on the north side of east-west roads".

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. BLOCK_USES (city_gen.gd:634-640) is cycled with kinds[k % kinds.size()] (661). Only the mall breaks after one building (675-678). Rows are filled from inner.position (656-679). The gaps are 6-12 in x and 7-10 in y. In 00_zone_map I counted NW 4x4 = 16 (8 hospitals, 4 flats, 4 offices), NE 5x4 = 20 (10 offices, 10 flats) and the W hospital block 3 (2 hospitals, 1 flats). With 2 malls and 4 market sheds that makes 45 slabs, 10 of them hospitals. All 8 military hospitals get the sign 'โรงพยาบาลทหาร' (698). The block areas sum to 98,896 cells, of which 65,703 are compound use. 04 and 06 do look like a business park.
verdicts.reason: The fact is right and it is the largest share of the land. ROADMAP.md:312 still lists 'อาคารเฉพาะในโซนอนุสาวรีย์ชัย' as open; round 4 built generic big buildings, not specific ones. However, the suggestion 'fill from the south edge so fronts face the road' collides with L3, which puts a shophouse strip on that same south edge. Both cannot own that edge.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Keep (1) the per-block "kinds" list in victory.cfg, with no modulo cycling and a stop when the list is placed; this is data plus about 10 lines in _big_block. Keep (5): per-building names. Reconcile (2) with L3: on a block north of an E-W road, pack the one main building against the south edge, leave a gate and drop-off gap to the road in front of it, and let the L3 shophouse strip run either side of that gap. Annexes and flats go behind it, and lawns and car parks go on the NORTH side of the plots. That also keeps the tall roofs, which rise 8-11 cells in 3/4 view, from covering the street behind (see missed M1). Target counts: military block 1 hospital + 1 ward block + 2 flats; W block 1 hospital; NE 3 offices + 1-2 condos. Make "wards" a flag on the hospital kind, not a new kind: skip the lobby and pharmacy in _corridor. Wait on "carpark" until siphoning exists (ROADMAP line 229, not done). Do it in the same GEN bump as L2, L3 and M1.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. Cross-sois start every 12-16 cells and run the full block height (city_gen.gd:762-766), so segments are 9-13 wide. Walking _row (797-826) by hand: a 9-wide segment gives 1 shop plus a 1-cell alley, and 11-13 wide gives 2. Every row gets a 3-cell soi (782). review.summary: Where the city can be seen, it already feels Thai. Shopfronts at play zoom (art_01), interiors (17-21) and the Victory Monument set pieces (01, 16) are specific and charming. The drawing pipeline is also solid: MeshCanvas batching, chunked ground and hash-based variety. The main problem is what the camera actually gets. The 3/4 projection lifts every roof 58-82 px (3.6-5 cells), and 84-180 px on big buildings, over 3-cell sois and sidewalks. Roughly two thirds of a wide frame is flat roof, many ground-floor shopfronts are hidden by the next row, and zombies on the sidewalk behind a building are invisible even when in line of sight (art_03). Occlusion should be fixed first: soi width against facade height, silhouettes for hidden people, and a cutaway instead of a whole-building fade. That matters more than any extra detail. After that, the cheapest wins are cleaning the ground noise (per-cell checker, black drains, grey squares in lawns), separating roof and ground values and adding building shadows, and filling roofs with real Bangkok rooftop life.
strengths: Shopfronts read as real Bangkok at the default zoom 4 (art_01): a Thai sign band in trade colours (building_prop.gd:26-33), a rolling shutter with its box, awnings, a barber pole or pharmacy cross, lightbox/flag/menu decor, scooters parked in front, bars on the windows, rain streaks.

Storytelling is layered into the drawing: rescue X-codes, Thai graffiti, SOS bedsheets, rooftop tarp camps, boarded windows (building_prop.gd:393-429, 245-258), and furniture that looks emptier once searched.

Interiors follow real layouts: the shop at the front, stairs in the middle, the back kitchen with a water jar (โอ่ง), a squat toilet, and wooden-floored bedrooms upstairs (17-19). Big buildings have wards, corridors, wheelchairs and lift doors (20-21).

The zone is recognisable from above (16): the monument with its five bronze figures and bayonet obelisk (street_prop.gd:634-667), the BTS curving round the circle, the skywalk ring, the station name board, and the canal with water hyacinth.
Night has real mood: lit windows, sodium lamp pools, the player's light and the BTS shadow (13, art_06).
Big-building facades differ by kind (hospital green bands and cross sign, office ribbon glazing, flats with balconies and laundry, mall banners). Rooftop tanks are tied to the water system.

Drawing is performance-aware and deterministic: MeshCanvas batches static shapes into one draw call, ground is chunked, overhead wires are split into pieces, and variety comes from hash01, so every client draws the same city.

findings.title: Front sois are narrower than the roofs that overhang them, so the next row hides the shopfronts
findings.observation: Rows face south onto 3-cell sois (SOI_W=3, city_gen.gd:28; rows and sois laid out at 774-783). A shophouse's facade lift h is 58 px for 2 storeys and 82 px for 3 (building_prop.gd:57-58, origin at the footprint bottom :59). The soi is only 48 px. So the roof of the row to the south covers the whole soi, plus 10 px (2-storey neighbour) or 34 px (3-storey neighbour) of the northern row's 30 px ground floor. With a 3-storey neighbour, a shop's shutter, awning and door are never visible from outside. In art_05 (zoom 1), no east-west soi is visible anywhere. The crop of its facade band shows three facades as windows + sign band, then roof straight away, with no ground floor. Estimate from the geometry: roofs are about 65% of the frame, facades about 17%, ground about 18%. The same shows in 10 (right column: the roof touches the facade) and 09. On avenues, the row south of the road faces away, so its roof hangs over the sidewalk and 1-2 lanes (11, art_03, bottom of 12). The south side of Ratchawithi has no shopfronts at all.
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:28, 774-783, 797-826; building_prop.gd:53-59; art_05_rows_z1 (facade band y 200-320), 10_shophouse_e right column, 09, 11_play_zoom, art_03_roof_hides_zombies_z4
findings.why: The ground floor is the most Thai and most useful thing in the city: sign, shutter, door, what the shop sells. With it hidden, players navigate by roof colour and can't tell a pharmacy from a gold shop from the street. Real sois are lined with fronts, so this hurts both realism-first and the choose-where-to-scavenge loop.
findings.suggestion: In CityGen._shophouse_block, split the soi a row faces from the back alley. Make the front soi at least ceil(h_south/16)+2 cells: 5 cells if the row south of it is capped at 2 storeys (cheapest: force rec.floors=2 for rows whose north side is a front soi; allow 3 only where an avenue or lot is to the north), or 6-7 cells otherwise. Make back-to-back rows share a 2-cell drain alley. That is also the real Bangkok pattern: fronts on a 6-8 m soi, backs on a narrow alley. For avenues, add a north-facing prefab variant (plan rows flipped: shutter row at the top) for rows whose north edge is a road. Draw it as roof plus a street edge: an awning strip hanging past the roof edge, a sign on the parapet, goods on the sidewalk. Then both sides of Ratchawithi read as shop streets. Cost: about 15% fewer rows per block. Needs a GEN bump and a new test_city fingerprint.

findings.why: Danger the rules say you can see, but the picture doesn't show, means unfair bites. Teammates also vanish behind buildings. This breaks the 'meet danger, decide' beat that the core loop depends on.
findings.suggestion: Add an occluded-people pass in Main._draw_fx (fx is z_index 3, main.gd:159, drawn above buildings). For each zombie or player with sight_k > 0.05 on your floor (_on_view_floor): if some BuildingProp in world.near(pos, 2) is visible, not in `faded`, has pos.y < b.position.y and b.visual_rect().has_point(pos + Vector2(0, -12)), draw a flat silhouette. Use a 8x26 rounded rect plus a head circle at pos + Vector2(0, -lift). Colour: Color(0.85, 0.3, 0.25, 0.5*sight_k) for zombies, Color(0.6, 0.8, 1, 0.5) for players. About 25 lines, nothing redrawn in the world. It only affects people, which fits the rule that only people fade.

findings.title: The roof fade turns a whole building into a ghost box and x-rays its rooms
findings.observation: _fade_trees_near sets modulate.a = 0.3 on every building whose visual rect touches your body (main.gd:1314-1318). Roof, facade and sign all drop to 30% at once. Underneath, the ground chunk's floor plan (FLOOR/IWALL tiles) and the separate DoorProp/FurnitureProp/DecorProp nodes (world.gd:146-211) stay fully drawn. So you see a neighbour's room layout, doors and water jars through the roof. Examples: art_01 bottom half, where two brown doors and a jar float in the soi; 11, a translucent brown slab with the curb, a tree and a parasol showing through; 03, a translucent rectangle over most of the canal; the bottom of 06.
findings.why: The frame loses its main shapes exactly where the player is looking. It also shows the loot layout of buildings you haven't entered yet.
findings.suggestion: Leave modulate at 1. Instead, give faded buildings a shared ShaderMaterial (set b.material while faded, null afterwards). In vertex(), pass the world position: (MODEL_MATRIX * vec4(VERTEX, 0.0, 1.0)).xy. In fragment(): COLOR.a *= mix(0.15, 1.0, smoothstep(r, r + 16.0, distance(world_pos, hole_center))), with r about 34 px and hole_center = me.position + Vector2(0, -14), set once per frame from _fade_trees_near. You get a soft window onto yourself and about 2 m around you; the rest of the roof, the facade and the sign stay solid. The glow child keeps its own unshaded material. The same shader can replace the whole-node fade on trees (main.gd:1302-1307) and the BTS pieces.

findings.title: Roofs are the main surface of the city and they are nearly empty
findings.observation: At zoom 1-2.5, roofs cover about two thirds of the frame (art_05, 09, 10). At play zoom, one shophouse roof (6-7 x 13-15 cells, about 100x230 px) fills most of the screen height (11, art_03). _flat_roof (building_prop.gd:163-207) gives each roof one flat tone (6 tones, :175) or plain corrugation, then 4 soft stains, one 12x8 patch, 1-3 AC units of 7x5 px, and maybe a tank, antenna or laundry line. That is well under 5% of the area. Nothing shows the prefab's stairs to the roof ('↑ ดาดฟ้า' in 19) or the back kitchen. Big roofs (_big_roof :637-696) are bigger still and just as bare (04 top-left, 05 top-right, 06 right): a 3-cell slab grid and a few tanks. About 6% of roofs carry the same 'SOS' (:246-250); art_05 shows two in one frame.
findings.why: Most pixels of the city say nothing. Shophouse rows read as a mosaic of coloured rectangles, not Bangkok, where rooftops are the busiest thing in any aerial photo.
findings.suggestion: Build each shophouse roof from its plan. Use the existing `extra` RNG so no other detail moves. (1) A stair hut (ป้อมบันได) with a door at the building's stair cell. In World._spawn_props, put the world.stairs cells inside rec.rect into data, then draw the hut like the big-roof stairwells (:656-660). (2) A rear extension: draw the last 3-4 rows as a lower rusty corrugated lean-to, with a 4-6 px step (a strip of back wall with a small window). That is the back kitchen from the prefab. (3) A 2 px light party-wall parapet plus a 1 px shadow between units, so rows get a rhythm. (4) A clutter budget by area (n = w*d/900) drawn from a weighted table: blue or stainless tanks, AC rows, a potted garden on the front third, a bamboo drying rack with laundry, a bird cage, a tarp room, an old sofa, a satellite dish, a corrugated add-on room (ห้องต่อเติม). Place it in bands away from the hut. (5) Vary the messages: SOS, ช่วยด้วย, มีคน 3, arrows, a name. For big roofs, go by kind: mall = rooftop car park (painted bays, 4-8 cars, ramp), hospital = HVAC plant and skylights, flats = washing lines and rows of tanks, office = penthouse and solar panels.

findings.title: Ground tiles show a 16 px checkerboard and black 'holes'
findings.observation: _draw_tile fills each cell with one flat colour: base.lightened(noise*0.05, or 0.12 on grass, + hash*0.03) (world.gd:1036). So asphalt, soi and grass show visible cell squares (enlarged crop of 12: 48 px blocks on Ratchawithi; the grass in 03; the lawns in 05). SOI cells get a near-black 8x5 drain (2e2c2a on 6b6862) on 3% of cells, at a fixed offset (world.gd:1112-1113). There are eleven in a 640x300 crop of 08, and five at zoom 4 in art_04, where each is a 32x20 px black bar. Big-block lawns are only 85% grass (city_gen.gd:693) laid over a SOI fill (:683). That leaves 1-cell grey squares all over the lawns (04, 05, 06, 07) and speckle on the zone map (00).
findings.evidence: world.gd:1036, 1071-1078, 1112-1113; city_gen.gd:683, 693; 12_ratchawithi (enlarged crop x0-640 y0-330); 08_market (crop x150-790 y0-300); art_04_big_front_z4 (5 black bars on the driveway); 05_hospital_block; 06_office; 07_mall; 00_zone_map
findings.why: This noise is the texture of every frame. Grid squares make the ground look tiled, and black rectangles read as holes or missing objects that compete with real threats.
findings.suggestion: (1) Add MeshCanvas.draw_quad4(a, b, c, d, ca, cb, cc, cd): 6 points with per-vertex colours, no triangulation. In _draw_tile, draw the base quad with corner colours sampled from the tint noise at (x,y), (x+1,y), (x+1,y+1), (x,y+1), and drop the per-cell hash term. Same cost, smooth mottling, no steps. (2) Drains: only on SOI/ROAD cells next to SIDEWALK or BUILDING (the kerb side). Draw them as a grate: frame base.darkened(0.15) with 3 slots base.darkened(0.35). (3) In the SOI branch, if 3 or more of the 4 neighbours are GRASS/TREE, draw the cell as worn grass (grass base darkened 0.1, a few dirt specks). This is drawing only, no GEN bump. (4) Where GRASS meets SOI/SIDEWALK/ROAD, draw a 2 px kerb (b8b2a4), so stepped lawn edges read as planters. Apply the same neighbour rule in city_map.gd so the M map loses the speckle.

findings.title: The default zoom shows one street and not what is coming
findings.observation: play_zoom 4 (main.gd:131) at 1280x720 frames 20 x 11 cells. In 11 that is 4.5 m of asphalt, the translucent roof slab and the HUD. In art_03 it is the far kerb and the roofs opposite. A zombie coming from the south appears about 5.5 m away, and the roofs remove another 3.6-5 m band behind every building (L1). Indoors, zoom 4 is right: shelves, fridges and signs are crisp (17, art_01). main.gd:1199 already blends zoom for roofs (want = play_zoom * lerpf(1.0, 0.78, roof_k)).
findings.why: Awareness drives 'meet danger, then decide'. The shape of the city (soi mouths, landmarks) is never in view at once, so walking outside feels like a corridor. That may feed the 'walk around, bored' feeling.
findings.suggestion: Use two zoom targets instead of one: outdoors 3.0 (27 x 15 m) and indoors 4 (today's). Blend them with the same lerp: want = play_zoom * lerpf(0.75, 1.0, inside_k) * lerpf(1.0, 0.78, roof_k), where inside_k eases toward 1 while hidden_building != null. Ctrl+wheel still scales both. Cost: the sight radius scales with zoom (main.gd:1178), so about 78% more area and characters are drawn. Measure with F3 on the web build before shipping, as the performance plan says.

findings.title: Roofs and walkable ground have the same value, and buildings cast no shadow
findings.observation: Concrete roof tones 6e6a63/7a746a/64625c/827a6c (building_prop.gd:175) sit on the same value as SOI 6b6862 (world.gd:38). Corrugated metal 8a8e90 (:167) is almost SIDEWALK 8e8a82 (world.gd:37). Only a 1.5 px outline at 20% black separates them (:192). Trees (tree_prop.gd:17-18) and vehicles (street_prop.gd:205-210, offsets to the right) cast shadows to the right; buildings cast none (the only 'shade' is behind the parapet, :214). In art_05 the north-south sois and the concrete roofs are the same grey. In 09 the soi at x 470-590 merges with the roofs on both sides.
findings.why: Telling at a glance where you can walk is the first job of top-down art. Without shadows, buildings look like flat decals rather than blocks with height.
findings.suggestion: (1) Move the roof tones a step lighter and warmer (e.g. 948e82, a09a8c, 8a8a80, 9aa48e painted green, b08470 painted red), and keep the ground darker and cooler, for a 12-15% value gap. (2) Draw cast shadows in World._draw_markings, which is one batch below all props. For each building, draw a band at its east edge: x = rect.end.x*T to + clamp(h*0.35, 8, 40), y = rect.position.y*T - h to rect.end.y*T, colour (0,0,0,0.2). Add a 3 px contact shadow along the facade base. Get h from a static BuildingProp.height_of(rec) (move the match at :42-58 into it). Also add a long thin wedge east of the monument obelisk and small shadows for the BTS pillars. The sun then agrees with the trees and cars, and north-south sois read as canyons.

findings.title: Interior walls read as black trenches, and every floor is the same terrazzo
findings.observation: IWALL tiles are flat 3a3632, with a 3 px 6e665c edge on every side that faces floor (world.gd:42, 1127-1131; upstairs 298-302). Furniture, by contrast, stands up with height (furniture_prop.gd TALL). So walls have no height while furniture does. The walls are about the value of asphalt and are the thickest dark shapes on screen: black bands down both sides of the shop in 17 and 18, a black grid in 20 and 21. All ground floors use FLOOR a89a82 terrazzo (world.gd:41, 1120-1126), so the pharmacy (17), hospital (20), mall (07) and market (08) have the same floor. A hanging bulb is a 16 px black line plus a dot (decor_prop.gd:92-94); with the roof off it reads as a pin stuck in the floor (17, 20).
findings.why: Scavenging happens indoors. Rooms should read instantly, and each kind of building should feel different (realism first).
findings.suggestion: (1) IWALL: fill with the building colour darkened 0.45 (via building_at[c].data.color). Draw only the south face: if c+DOWN is FLOOR, draw a 5 px strip at the bottom of the wall cell in the colour darkened 0.15, with a 1 px dark base line. That is the 3/4 face, matching the facades. Drop the edge on the other sides or make it 1 px. Do the same in _draw_upper. (2) Add a FLOOR_STYLE table keyed by building kind (plus 'bath' for cells near toilet decor): shop = terrazzo (as now); upstairs = boards (as now); hospital = pale mint vinyl in 2x2-cell squares; mall = cream polished 2x2 tiles with a faint sheen; office = grey carpet tiles; market = wet concrete with a drain channel; bathroom/kitchen = small blue-white tiles. (3) Bulb: draw only the bulb and a 3 px cord, plus a soft warm ellipse on the floor under it when it is lit.

findings.title: Night lighting ignores the dead grid, and dusk is a flat pink filter
findings.observation: Big buildings glow only when they have power (building_prop.gd:776-778). But every shop lights about 30% of its windows plus its sign every night (:791-799), and all street lamps switch on (street_prop.gd:104-114; main.gd:1076-1081). art_02 shows a lit window above a dead barber's shop; art_06 shows all of Phahon Yothin in sodium light. Dusk is a CanvasModulate multiply (SKY 18h (1.0, 0.80, 0.58), 19h (0.80, 0.55, 0.52), main.gd:1127-1132). In 14 the monument is uniformly pink with lower contrast, and lamps and glow don't start until light < 0.6.
findings.evidence: building_prop.gd:776-799; street_prop.gd:104-114; main.gd:1071-1081, 1127-1144; shaders/post.gdshader; art_02_front_z4_night; art_06_phahon_night_z2; 13_night_street; 14_evening_monument
findings.why: In a dead city, light should mean someone is there: a player's generator, a camp. Random lit windows erase the strongest co-op beacon. And golden hour is Bangkok's mood shot.
findings.suggestion: (1) Gate the 'shop' and 'condo' glow by data.lit, as big buildings already are, keeping all_lit for the title screen. Turn street lamps on only while a zone-wide grid flag is on. Tie that flag to the ROADMAP 'โลกเปลี่ยนตามวัน' timeline in a table (e.g. grid on for days 1-7). After that, only lamps near generators or the camp stay lit. Keep a rare candle flicker (about 1 window in 200, from a table) so the city isn't pitch black. (2) Replace the dusk multiply with split toning in post.gdshader: add shadow_tint and highlight_tint uniforms fed from two extra SKY columns (e.g. at 18h shadows (0.75, 0.72, 0.95), highlights (1.12, 0.95, 0.78)); then c = mix(c*shadow_tint, c*highlight_tint, smoothstep(0.15, 0.75, lum)). Fade signs and lamps in over 18:30-19:30 instead of switching at light < 0.6.

findings.title: The cable tangle draws across the player
findings.observation: Overhead is z_index 4 (world.gd:251), above every character. Its wires are 4-6 lines of 0.5-0.7 px at alpha 0.85 (overhead.gd:143-162). At zoom 4 they become 2-3 px dark lines that cut through a character on the sidewalk: in 11, the sagging wires cross the player's body at about y 370-410. The overhead node is faded only for the BTS and the skywalk (main.gd:1319-1339), never for wires.
findings.why: The character is the one thing that must always read clearly. The wires are atmosphere and should never hide it.
findings.suggestion: In Overhead._ready, keep a map from key to wire piece (the wires are already grouped by chunk key, overhead.gd:16-22). In _fade_trees_near, set modulate.a = 0.35 on the piece(s) with a wire within about 20 px of the body rect (Geometry2D.get_closest_point_to_segment on each wire's endpoints), and add them to `faded`. Optionally draw wires at 0.6 alpha when camera zoom is 3.5 or more.

findings.title: Every tree is the same tree
findings.observation: TreeProp draws one form: a trunk and 7 clumps, one green (3f5431 plus or minus 9%), radius 10-14 px x1.4 (tree_prop.gd:13-34). The lawns in 05, 06 and 07, the park beside Phahon Yothin (02) and the roundabout (01) are fields of identical bushes. The canopy is about 2.5 m in radius, smaller than the rain trees that shade Bangkok avenues.
findings.why: Greenery covers much of the non-shophouse blocks. Varying species and size is cheap realism, and it gives landmarks to navigate by.
findings.suggestion: Pick a species from hash01(cell, 60) and the surrounding tiles. Rain tree (ก้ามปู): wide flat canopy, radius x1.8, for cells within 4 of a ROAD. Coconut or royal palm: slim trunk and 6 radial fronds, for the roundabout island and medians. Banana clump: 4-5 big paddle leaves, on DIRT and vacant lots. Flame tree (หางนกยูง) or ราชพฤกษ์: the current shape with 10% red or yellow flower dots. Mango or tamarind: as today. Keep the shadow to the right, and scale the fade box in _fade_trees_near (main.gd:1302-1307) by species radius. This is derived from existing TREE cells, so no GEN change.

findings.title: The monument, the zone's signature landmark, is pixel-stepped inside smooth rings
findings.observation: The grass island and the paved plaza are _disk tile fills (city_gen.gd:201-203): 16 px staircases. Next to them, the kerb and lane line are smooth draw_arc (world.gd:1212-1216) and the skywalk is a smooth 72-segment ring (overhead.gd:122-139). The roundabout's outer edge is stepped too, so its red-white kerb paint follows a staircase (16: left and right corners; 01).
findings.why: This is the view people will screenshot and share (01, 14, 16). Mixing stepped and smooth shapes reads as a bug, not a style.
findings.suggestion: In World._draw_markings, before the arcs, draw smooth filled polygons (96 points) over the stepped tiles: grass colour at radius (island+0.5)*T, plaza colour at (island-3.5)*T. Add plaza joints (3 concentric rings and 16 radial lines) and a few tufts. For the outer edge, sample 128 angles. Where the tile at radius r+1.5 is SIDEWALK, draw an annulus quad from (r+0.5)*T to (r+2.5)*T in sidewalk colour and a dashed red/white kerb arc at (r+0.5)*T. In world.gd:1095-1104, skip the tile kerb paint for cells whose distance to circle.at is between r-1 and r+3. Tiles and collision stay as they are.

findings.title: Street level lacks the small Thai signs that also help players find their way
findings.observation: The dressing is good right outside shops (decor: lightbox, flag, menu, grill, plants; stalls, umbrellas, scooters, spirit houses, bus stops). But nothing names or marks a soi, and at zoom 4 (a 20 m view) frames are anonymous (11, art_03, 12). There are no soi-mouth signs, no motorbike-taxi (วินมอเตอร์ไซค์) stands, no vinyl banners on upper floors, and no blade signs sticking out from facades. Signs are a single flush band plus TALL_SIGNS (building_prop.gd:356-361, 366-377).
findings.why: With a 20 m view you find your way by landmarks. These are also the quickest-to-read Bangkok cues, drawn with a few rectangles.
findings.suggestion: Visual-only additions, not world records, so no GEN bump. (1) A blue soi sign 'ซ. N' (white text) on a post at every soi mouth onto a road. Compute them in World from tiles (a SOI cell touching SIDEWALK), number them along each road, and draw them in _draw_markings or a light node. The M map and quests can use the same numbers. (2) A motorbike-taxi stand at about a third of soi mouths, chosen by cell hash: a bench, a 'วิน' sign, orange vests on a rail. (3) In BuildingProp._draw_shop with `extra`: 15% of upper floors get a white vinyl banner (ให้เช่า / เซ้ง / ขาย plus a phone number), and 20% get a blade sign sticking out 1-2 px sideways at the sign band. Use parody names only, no brands.

findings.title: No fixed art snapshot to compare before and after
findings.observation: Generation has a fingerprint test (tests/test_city.gd), but the look has no regression check. This review had to write ad-hoc scripts (city_review_shots.gd, art_shots.gd in the scratchpad) that host on a test port, move the camera and save PNGs. Every item above is visual tuning that needs side-by-side comparison.
findings.evidence: tests/test_city.gd; scratchpad city_review_shots.gd and art_shots.gd (both follow test_base.gd host()/go()/shot())
findings.why: A solo developer tuning art needs a quick before/after loop. Otherwise changes to one view (e.g. roof tones) quietly break another (night, interiors).
findings.suggestion: Check in tests/art_shots.gd (not part of run_all): about 12 fixed spots covering zoom 4 front, zoom 4 avenue, zoom 1 rows, monument, interior, night, dusk and a hidden-zombie setup, written to user://art_shots/<date>/. Add a one-line command in ROADMAP. Optional: a tiny HTML contact sheet comparing the last two runs.

verdicts.fact_check: Checked city_gen.gd:774-783. Each row is 13-15 cells deep and is followed by a SOI_W=3 east-west soi, repeated down the block. Every row faces south (prefab README says 'street at the bottom'; ROADMAP:139 'หันใต้'), so each soi is the front of the row to its north and the back of the row to its south. There is no separate back alley. building_prop.gd:59 puts the origin at the footprint bottom, and _flat_roof (:164) draws the roof from footprint-top minus h to footprint-bottom minus h, so the roof overhangs h px to the north. Shops are 2 or 3 storeys, 50/50 (city_gen.gd:378), giving h = 58 or 82 px against a 48 px soi. The roof therefore covers the whole soi plus 10 or 34 px of the next row's 30 px ground floor. This shows in art_05 (no east-west soi visible, several facades cut off at the sign band), 10 (right column) and 15 (gold-shop shutter cut). An extra fact makes it worse: the trade dressing from _shop_fronts (city_gen.gd:1186-1202) is placed in the first soi cell (y = r.end.y), which is always under the southern neighbour's roof. You only see it through your own fade (art_01).
verdicts.reason: The fact is right, and it is the main reason the streets don't read as Bangkok. But back-to-back rows need north-facing shops, and this projection draws only south faces. A north-facing front would sit invisible under its own roof. That means large work (flipped prefabs, shutters and doors on the north wall, new facade drawing) for little visible gain. The width rule is also inconsistent: ceil(58/16)+2 is 6, not 5.
verdicts.revised_observation: Every east-west soi is 3 cells (48 px) and is both the front of one row and the back of the next. The southern row's roof (58 px for 2 storeys, 82 px for 3) covers the whole soi and the bottom 10 or 34 px of the northern row's 30 px ground floor. The result: no soi ground is visible at any zoom, 3-storey neighbours hide shutters and doors completely, and the FRONTS pavement dressing is always under a roof.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) Add FRONT_SOI := 5 in CityGen and use it only for the east-west sois at city_gen.gd:782-783. Keep SOI_W 3 for the north-south cross-sois (:765). (2) Keep the rng.randi_range(2, 3) draw at :378 so the random stream doesn't shift, then set rec.floors = 2 for shops. This also removes the phantom third storey (missed M1). With h 58 and an 80 px soi, every shopfront, its FRONTS dressing and a 22 px strip of soi are visible. It costs about 10% of the rows. (3) Optional, for avenues: where a block's north edge is a road, start the first row 4 cells in (a SOI back lane), so the sidewalk on the south side of east-west roads stays visible. Skip north-facing prefabs. Needs GEN 10 and a new test_city fingerprint.

verdicts.fact_check: Verified the geometry. A zombie at rect.y-1 has its feet about 8 px north of the footprint and its body reaches about 34 px up. The roof reaches 58-82 px north, and the BuildingProp (z 1, world.gd:139; y = footprint bottom, building_prop.gd:59) sorts after the zombie (z 1, main.gd:396), so the roof draws over it. The sight system counts the zombie as seen (main.gd:1181-1182). Only buildings that touch the local player's body fade (main.gd:1308-1318). One correction: other players are not fully lost, because their name tag is drawn on fx (z 3) with sight_k alpha (main.gd:1345-1352). Zombies get nothing. The case is also stronger than the sidewalk example: every cell of a 3-cell east-west soi is under the southern row's roof, so a zombie coming down a soi is invisible except under the one 6-7-cell unit that fades around you.
verdicts.reason: This has the biggest effect on play and is cheap to fix. The per-zombie test can be cheaper than scanning world.near().
verdicts.revised_observation: Zombies anywhere in a 3-cell east-west soi, and on sidewalks behind a row, are drawn under roofs even though sight counts them as visible (sight_k 1). Only the one building touching your own body fades. Teammates keep their fx name tag, but zombies vanish completely. Big buildings hide a 7-11-cell strip.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: In Main._draw_fx, for each zombie with sight_k > 0.05 that passes _on_view_floor, walk the cells south of it. For k in 1..12, take b = world.building_at.get(cell + Vector2i(0, k)). The zombie is hidden if b exists, b.visible, not faded.has(b), and b.h > k*16 - 20 (the roof reaches its head). If so, draw a flat silhouette (a rounded body plus a head circle, Color(0.85, 0.3, 0.25, 0.45*sight_k)) at z.position + Vector2(0, -z.lift). That is about 20 lines and only dictionary lookups. Skip players, since they already have tags. Keep this even after L1, because big buildings still hide 7-11 cells.

verdicts.fact_check: main.gd:1317 sets modulate.a = 0.3 on the whole BuildingProp, and roof, facade and sign are one MeshCanvas batch. Interior FLOOR/IWALL tiles live in the ground chunks (world.gd:1120-1131), and doors, furniture and decor are separate nodes that sort before the building (world.gd:146-211), so they all show through. Confirmed in 03_canal (a 6-storey roof as a see-through slab covering most of the canal), the bottom of art_01 (doors and a water jar of the building south of the soi), 11, and the bottom of 06.
verdicts.reason: The fact is right. But a canvas shader is new ground for a beginner, and a 34 px circular hole shows less of the soi than today's full-width fade, so you would lose the view down the soi. Best done after X1.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: First, a one-line step: raise modulate.a from 0.3 to 0.5. That means less x-ray, and the player is still readable. Then build the proposed hole shader, but make the hole an ellipse of about 64x40 px (wider than tall) around the body, so the soi stays visible on both sides. The glow child keeps its own unshaded material. Anyone outside the hole relies on the X1 silhouettes.

verdicts.fact_check: Checked _flat_roof (building_prop.gd:163-207) and _roof_life (:211-258). Even with every extra, a shop roof carries only about 3-8 small items on about 100x220 px (art_05, 09). SOS appears on about 6% of roofs (:247) and 'ช่วยด้วย' on 3%. Big roofs do have stairwell huts, a lift room, AC rows and tank stands (:637-696), but the items are sparse for the area. The stair cell is already on the record (rec.stairs, city_gen.gd:606), so there is no need to pass world.stairs in. The rear lean-to conflicts with the plans: every prefab's floor 2 covers the full depth, with bedrooms over the kitchen (pharmacy.txt and home.txt, floor 2 rows 2-4 'Wb..cW'), and players walk on the roof at height h (world.gd:903-905).
verdicts.reason: The roofs are sparse, but this is less urgent. After L1 roofs take a smaller share of the frame, and at the default zoom 4 you see only 1-2 roofs. The lean-to part is wrong for the interiors.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) Draw a stair hut (ป้อมบันได) over data.stairs, like the big-roof stairwells (:656-660). It also shows a player on the roof where the way down is. (2) Add a party-wall parapet line plus a 1 px shadow at each unit's edge, so rows get a rhythm.
