review.summary: The city has strong foundations: WorldState diffs, state worked out from the clock instead of ticked, zombies dressed and typed by place, trapped zombies in big buildings, and loot tables driven by data. But the city itself does little in play. Outside big buildings, every zombie comes from a 40-zombie bubble that follows each player. That bubble ignores the place and forgets kills. Most noises are too short to reach past the ring where new zombies appear. Food and water are in every house, any rain refills every rooftop tank, and nothing changes as days pass. So where you go and where you live hardly matters, which fits the 'walk around, bored' feeling. The best changes: a zombie population per block with noise heat, a real-time season clock with stages, concentrating value and danger by place (army, hospital, shut shutters), and quests that point at places. Before 20-50 players share a zone, the search-once loot and the 4-minute day (as a clock for the 'days later' story) need a plan.
strengths: Zombies already belong to places: outfit and kind come from the block they spawn in (items.gd:372-466, zombie.gd:584-603). Guards whistle in offices, the mall and hospitals, fakers lie in hospitals, aerobics dancers stay in the mall. This is the right base for danger that depends on the place.

Trapped zombies are just a number per big building: they are let out when someone comes near, and every kill lowers the number for good (buildings.gd:37-46, survival.gd:513-584). It costs little CPU, it persists, and it makes big-building loot cost something. The same trick can carry a population per block.

State is worked out from the clock, not counted every frame (rooftop tanks, generator fuel, fridges, stoves: buildings.gd:14-18, things.gd:125-133, items.gd:549-575), and WorldState keeps only what differs from the start. Season stages and population regrowth can use the same pattern for almost no CPU or bandwidth.

Systems already clash in the way ROADMAP asks for: a generator gives light, cold fridges and a water pump, but it is loud (things.gd:288-298, 344-363). Street-lamp pools against dark sois change how far zombies see you, 120 px vs 55 px (zombie.gd:71-72, world.gd:491-499). That gives real choices of route at night.

Loot is rolled in two steps (what the furniture holds, tipped by the kind of place, then rarity), so adding new items never makes the basics rarer (items.gd:616-698). A shop's sign decides its loot table (city_gen.gd:42-50), so the front of a shop tells you what is inside.

Making a home safe works from start to finish: rolling shutters (loud, 150 hp per section), up to 3 boards per door or window, a better night's sleep in a building shut tight, and waking up at your own bed after death (doors.gd, survival.gd:89-104).

The zone is drawn by hand from OpenStreetMap, with named roads and blocks and a `use` for each block (victory.cfg:11-48). Game systems can read this data, and it matches the 'recognisable Bangkok' goal.

findings.title: Zombies are a bubble around players, not a population of places; most noise can't reach beyond it
findings.observation: Outside big buildings, every zombie is spawned 320-840 px (20-52 m) from a random living player, until 40 are within 900 px of that player (survival.gd:453-475, main.gd:12-13). Zombies more than 1350 px from everyone are dropped (survival.gd:483-498). There is no place factor: a soi, the market and the roundabout get the same density. Kills don't last. The daily quest 'เคลียร์ซอย' (quests.cfg:72-77) promises a quieter home tonight, but the cap refills at one zombie every 5 s by day and every 1.5 s at night (main.gd:610-616). Idle zombies walk at random and stand still 60% of the time (zombie.gd:220-223, 262). They see 120 px by day and 55 px in the dark (zombie.gd:71-72). How far noise carries: walk 45, run 115, hit 130, break 170, generator 190, smashing a vending machine 200, screamer 260, whistle 300 px (main.gd:64-69, things.gd:38-39 and 331, survival.gd:319-322). Every one except the whistle is shorter than the 320 px minimum spawn distance, and noise only reaches zombies that already exist (main.gd:677-684).
findings.evidence: survival.gd:453-498; main.gd:12-13, 64-69, 606-616, 677-684; zombie.gd:71-72, 220-262; things.gd:38-39, 331; quests.cfg:72-77; 11_play_zoom (at the default zoom the street on screen is empty)
findings.why: What makes this genre exciting is choosing a risk: the loud way or the quiet way, the busy market or the dead soi, clearing the streets round your home. Today none of these choices changes what happens, so the city feels like scenery. This is probably the main systems cause of 'walk around, bored'.
findings.suggestion: Give each block a zombie population number, using the same 'a number until someone comes near' trick as trapped zombies. (1) Data: add "density" to every block in data/zones/victory.cfg:39-48, e.g. market 1.6, mall grounds 1.3, roundabout and avenues 1.2, hospital grounds 1.0, shophouse sois 0.8. (2) Add a WorldState kind "block" {pop, pop_at}, starting at area × density. _spawn_zombie picks a cell, finds its block, and only spawns if that block still has pop left. Combat kills do pop - 1, like Survival.trapped_died. Pop grows back by the clock, worked out when asked like Buildings.tank, so clearing the soi round your home lasts hours. (3) Noise heat: Main.stimulus also adds radius/100 to a per-chunk heat dictionary that decays each game minute. _spawn_zombie favours cells in the direction of high heat and calls z.sense(noise_pos, long look), so zombies walk in from beyond the ring. Generators, vending machines, gunshots and screamers then have a real price. Keep the measured on-screen budget of 40-60 zombies as the ceiling.

findings.title: Value by place is flat: essentials are in every house, and dangerous places hold nothing special
findings.observation: Water, instant noodles and canned fish are found in store, food and home (items.cfg:276, 288). 'home' is also the fallback for any category (items.gd:703-710). So the kitchen and bedroom of each of the ~260 shophouses feeds you (estimate from 00_zone_map). Antibiotics (cure 60) are uncommon in every pharmacy and clinic shophouse (items.cfg:263-275), and those have 0 trapped zombies (buildings.gd:42-44). Pistol, shotgun, ammo9 and shells have no `places` at all (items.cfg:2047-2110), so guns never appear. The military hospital block uses the same hospital/flats/office plans and tables as the civilian hospital and the office block (city_gen.gd:634-640). On 00_zone_map the NW and NE quadrants look alike. The army checkpoint (city_gen.gd:1141-1163) is sandbags and a truck with nothing to search. Gold (items.cfg:574) has no use yet.
findings.evidence: items.gd:639-656, 703-710; items.cfg:263-288, 574, 2047-2110; buildings.gd:42-44; city_gen.gd:634-640, 1141-1163; 00_zone_map (NW and NE compounds nearly the same); 04_mil_hospital vs 06_office
findings.why: Players take risks when something they want can only be found somewhere dangerous. ROADMAP already wants a ladder of difficulty: บ้านแถว < ห้าง/ตลาด < โรงพยาบาล < ฐานทหาร. Today the safest shophouse gives almost everything you need.
findings.suggestion: Mostly table changes. (a) Add an 'army' place in Items.PLACES with rows: ammo9 and shells (uncommon), pistol (rare), stab vest, army ration, batteries. Give it to a 'guardpost/armory' room role in BigPlans._role when the block use is military_hospital (one per building), and to a container on the checkpoint's army truck. Add a DRESS 'army' set (fatigues, helmet) for those zombies and use kind 'guard'. (b) Tier the medicine: syringe and firstaid only in hospitals (move firstaid out of 'med'); antibiotics rare in pharmacies and uncommon in hospitals. (c) Collect the essentials in their proper places: PLACE_BIAS home = {food 0.6, drink 0.6}, while minimarts, eateries and the market keep full weight. (d) Let the empty chance depend on the place, not only the furniture: med 0.5 and store 0.45 ('raided first'), hospital 0.1. This is read at search time, so no GEN bump. (e) Build the gradient around the planned refugee camp: safe near it, more dangerous further out (see S1 density). Cost to note: this zone has no wat block, so the camp needs a place, either a small added wat or the military hospital lawn as an army-run evacuation point (keep the generic name 'โรงพยาบาลทหาร'). Only the checkpoint and armory containers need a GEN bump; (b)-(d) are runtime only.

findings.title: Nothing ages: no 'Days Later' arc, and a 4-minute day can't carry one
findings.observation: DAY_LENGTH is 240 s (main.gd:10). A server running 24/7 passes ~360 game days per real day, with a horde every 3 game days, which is every 12 real minutes (survival.gd:24, 371-373). ROADMAP's arc (week 1 power, week 2 dark: ROADMAP.md:390) would be over in under an hour of server time. No system reads 'time since the outbreak'. Street lamps light the night forever (world.gd:494-499: only room bulbs check power). No building has power without a big-building generator (buildings.gd:100-108). Taps depend only on rain (buildings.gd:69-74). Perishable loot is always 0-50% through its life measured from now (inventory.gd:600-602). Trapped zombies and searched containers only ever go down. The intro quest says 'day 3, the power is still on, the water still runs' (quests.cfg:31), but the systems say the opposite. The HUD shows 'วันที่ 1' (11_play_zoom); on a server this becomes a 4-5 digit number.
findings.evidence: main.gd:10-11; survival.gd:24, 371-386; world.gd:491-499; buildings.gd:69-74, 100-108; inventory.gd:600-602; quests.cfg:31; ROADMAP.md:390; 11_play_zoom (วันที่ 1)
findings.why: The name promises a city that runs down. A world that changes is also what makes a season worth logging into again, and what forces 'move or invest' decisions about your home (ROADMAP.md:343). It needs a clock other than the day/night one.
findings.suggestion: Add a season clock separate from day/night: real seconds the zone server has run with at least one player on, saved in world.save. Add a table data/eras.cfg keyed on season days, e.g. {0: grid on, mains water on}, {3: grid off}, {7: mains water off}, {14: shelves thinner, perishables found rotten}, {30: overgrowth, more fakers}. Readers: Buildings.powered (true for every building while the grid is on, which lights every bulb and fridge), Buildings.tank (mains refill), World.is_lit (skip street lamps when the grid is off), Items.roll (extra empty chance by stage), inventory.gd:600 (`made` measured from the outbreak, not from now). Announce each stage on the radios (Things 'radio') and with the existing fx_announce. Show the survivor's own days alive in the HUD instead of the server day. Runtime only, no GEN bump.

findings.title: Searched once, empty forever: a 20-50 player zone runs dry in hours, and first come takes all
findings.observation: A container's loot is rolled once, and the 'searched' flag is saved forever (inventory.gd:589-613, save_game.gd:95-104). Trapped zombies only ever go down (survival.gd:579-584). Awake, hunger empties in 1200 real seconds and thirst in 720 (survival.gd:11-14). Noodles give 40, fish cans 30, a water bottle 45, so each player uses about 8 food and 11 drink items per real hour. Estimate: ~260 shophouses × ~10 containers each (home.txt) plus ~45 big buildings with hundreds each is on the order of 10,000 containers, each giving 1-3 items (items.gd:677-698). 50 players eat about 1,000 food and drink items per hour, so the zone's food lasts roughly one day of busy play, not a 2-3 month season (ROADMAP.md:345). One jackpot room: each mall's supermarket is ~90 shelf containers plus a wall of fridges (big_plans.gd:313-322; 07_mall), about 150-200 food and drink items for whoever arrives first.
findings.evidence: inventory.gd:578-613; save_game.gd:95-104; survival.gd:11-14, 579-584; items.gd:677-698; big_plans.gd:313-322; data/prefabs/home.txt; 07_mall (rows of supermarket shelves); ROADMAP.md:345, 405-406
findings.why: Online, the city is shared. Without restocking, early players strip the zone and later ones find an empty shell. That kills 'go out to scavenge', which is the first step of the core loop. ROADMAP already says this must exist before going online.
findings.suggestion: Make ROADMAP's 'budget' restock concrete. Store searched_at (real time) instead of a bool. Every 10 minutes the server picks up to K containers that were searched more than 6 real hours ago, in buildings with no player within 2×NEAR and not claimed as a home, and marks them unsearched again, keeping anything players left inside. K is a per-zone budget, e.g. 60 per hour scaled by players online. The roll uses the season stage (S3), so late restocks lean toward junk, materials and canned food. Big buildings slowly regain trapped zombies (people who sheltered there and turned). Tame the jackpot rooms: raise the empty chance for 'store' inside a mall to ~0.7, or merge each supermarket aisle into one container. Needs a save VERSION bump, not a GEN bump.

findings.title: Quests and the map don't point anywhere, so the new quest system doesn't use the city
findings.observation: Quest objective kinds have no location (quests.gd:51-52). note() only filters on 'kind' and 'item' (quests.gd:104-107), and searching reports no place (inventory.gd:591). Daily quests are kill, search, cook or board anywhere (quests.cfg:72-126). The M map shows no street or block names, although victory.cfg names every road and block (victory.cfg:11-19, 39-48). Its legend lists วัด and คอนโด, which this zone doesn't have, and hospitals, the mall and the market get the same brown as everything else (city_map.gd:43, 240-241).
findings.why: Quests are the agreed fix for boredom, and they are the cheapest way to send players across a gradient of danger. Right now they can all be done in the first shophouse.
findings.suggestion: (a) Pass {place, block} to quests.note for searches (inventory.gd:591), and add optional 'place' and 'block' filters to note(). Add kinds 'visit' (enter a named block), 'power' (start a generator) and 'fill' (water from the canal, a jar or a tap). Add rows such as 'ร้านยาแถวราชปรารภ: ค้นร้านขายยา 3 ตู้', 'ตลาดซอยรางน้ำ: หาข้าวสาร 1 กระสอบ', 'ไฟในโรงพยาบาลทหาร: ติดเครื่องปั่นไฟ', 'น้ำคลองสามเสน: ตักน้ำ 3 ส่วน'. Weight the daily pool toward places the player hasn't explored yet (the map's fog data already knows). (b) On the map, draw road and block names from the zone data, colour hospital, mall, market and office buildings, and build the legend only from what exists in the zone.

findings.title: Shut shutters, rescue X-marks and warning graffiti are only decoration; make them true
findings.observation: Half the shophouses have their shutter down (rec.open 50%: city_gen.gd:375, 533-539). Opening one is loud (NOISE_HIT, doors.gd:147-159), and each section has 150 hp (world.gd:18). But the chance of finding loot depends only on the furniture (items.gd:655-656, 677-679), and no shophouse has trapped zombies (buildings.gd:42-44). Facades draw 'ไม่มีของแล้ว' (nothing left), 'อย่าเข้า' (keep out), 'ติดเชื้อ' (infected) and rescue-team X-marks with a 'found inside' count at random (building_prop.gd:34, 416-429). None of it matches what is inside.
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:375, 529-540; doors.gd:145-159; items.gd:655-656; buildings.gd:42-44; building_prop.gd:34, 393-429; 10_shophouse_e (orange X-mark on the clinic's shutter), 09_shophouse_sw (graffiti and shutters down)
findings.why: Reading the street at play zoom and choosing is the Zomboid/DayZ pleasure: a quiet, already-looted open shop, or a loud shutter with food behind it and a family of zombies. It adds real risk and reward to the ~260 shophouses that would otherwise be identical, with almost no new art. It also covers the horror-roadmap items 'ซอมบี้ติดในตึก' and 'ทุบประตูจากข้างใน'.
findings.suggestion: Write one building-facts function, e.g. Buildings.story(rec), from rec.seed and rec.open with no new random draws. (a) Shutter-down shophouses: 30% hold 1-3 trapped zombies (the family). Remove the `big` filter in trapped_start (buildings.gd:43) and _tick_trapped (survival.gd:520); _let_out already handles upper floors. They bang on the shutter when they hear you. (b) At search time in Items.roll: empty chance × 0.4 in shutter-down shops, × 2 in open-front ones (already looted). (c) Pick facade graffiti from the facts: the X-mark's lower number = trapped count, 'อย่าเข้า'/'ติดเชื้อ' only where trapped > 0, 'ไม่มีของแล้ว' only on looted shops. Runtime and drawing only, no GEN bump.

findings.title: A sealed home can get a zombie spawned inside it
findings.observation: _spawn_zombie only rejects cells that are out of bounds or solid (survival.gd:466-468). Shophouse and big-building floors are FLOOR, which is not solid (city_gen.gd:515-516, world.gd:603-606). The only other guard is staying 300 px from any player (survival.gd:469-472). A shophouse is at most 15 cells (240 px) deep, so while you scavenge 20-50 m from your boarded-up home, a zombie can appear inside it. spot_safe (survival.gd:91-104) then fails, and the home stops being safe although you did nothing wrong.
findings.why: 'Go home' is the anchor of the core loop, and home claiming comes next. If a shut, boarded house can fill up by itself, boarding feels pointless and players stop trusting the systems.
findings.suggestion: In survival.gd:467, also skip cells where w.building_at.has(c). If you want houses to fill up over time, allow it only in buildings with an open or broken door and no claimed bed, so it always has a cause the player can see. Zombies already get in through broken doors and windows by pathing.

findings.title: Water isn't scarce anywhere: any shower fills every rooftop tank, and the canal is far from homes
findings.observation: A tank holds 60 sips and rain adds 12 sips per game hour (buildings.gd:20-21); a game hour is 10 s (main.gd:11). The shortest rain (90 s, survival.gd:36) adds 108 sips, more than a full tank. About 70% of shophouses have a tap (things.gd:440), and each sip is worth 15 thirst (items.gd:513). So after any rain, every home is a near-endless water source. Khlong Sam Sen runs only along the top of the map (victory.cfg:28, rows 16-22), with compounds and grass on its banks (03_canal, 00_zone_map); the nearest shophouses are ~200 cells away. Realism: Bangkok rooftop tanks are filled from the mains by a pump, not by rain. Rain is caught in โอ่ง (water jars), and every shophouse plan except the minimart already has one ('J', city_gen.gd:62-67; home.txt row 2), but only as decoration.
findings.evidence: buildings.gd:20-22, 69-83; main.gd:10-11; survival.gd:30-36; things.gd:436-441; items.gd:511-515; victory.cfg:28; city_gen.gd:62-67; data/prefabs/*.txt ('J' in 11 of 12); 03_canal; 00_zone_map
findings.why: Water is the fastest need (a bar lasts 12 real minutes), so it should be what makes a home better or worse: a jar, near the canal, a big building with a cistern and a generator. Right now it makes no difference where you live.
findings.suggestion: (a) Tanks fill from the mains only while the season stage says the water is on (S3); after that, shophouse tanks only drain. Big buildings keep the pump-and-generator refill that already exists. Cut TANK_RAIN to a trickle. (b) Make the jar a Thing ('jar', state {water}), placed like place_stoves with no random draws (things.gd:461-464). Rain fills it at a real-time rate, e.g. 2 sips per real minute of rain up to 20. Scoop and drink like canal water, with a small sick chance. (c) Add a canal-side row of houses (ชุมชนริมคลอง) on the canal's south bank in victory.cfg, so 'live by the canal' is a real choice: water always, but an open, exposed towpath. (b) and (c) need a GEN bump and a new fingerprint; (a) is runtime.

findings.title: Homes run out of gas and fuel, and the street offers no way to resupply
findings.observation: A stove has 2-6 uses of gas, then says 'แก๊สหมดแล้ว' (out of gas) forever (things.gd:36, 105-113, 140-144). There is no gas-bottle item. Generator fuel only comes from uncommon jerrycans (items.cfg:781). The hundreds of parked cars, wrecks, vans, buses, tuk-tuks and street food carts (city_gen.gd:917-941, 1039-1041; 02_phahon_bts) can only be climbed (interact.gd:214-219, street_prop.gd:12). 'ค้นท้ายรถ' (search car boots) and 'ดูดน้ำมัน' (siphon fuel) are listed in ROADMAP but not built (ROADMAP.md:197, 229).
findings.evidence: things.gd:36, 99-144; items.cfg:781; interact.gd:214-219; street_prop.gd:12; city_gen.gd:917-941, 1039-1041; ROADMAP.md:197, 229; 02_phahon_bts and 08_market (streets full of carts and cars you can't use)
findings.why: This is the core loop in its purest form: something at home runs out, you go out for a specific heavy thing, you carry it back and use it. It also turns the most common Thai street furniture (food carts with LPG tanks, parked pickups) into play.
findings.suggestion: (a) Add a 'gasbottle' item (ถังแก๊ส, weight ~6 so it slows you), found in food and tools places, plus a one-shot 'ถอดถังแก๊ส' (take the gas tank) on every street food cart and eatery grill, stored as WorldState kind 'prop' {taken}. Add a stove action 'เปลี่ยนถังแก๊ส' (swap the gas tank) that sets gas = GAS[1]. (b) 'ดูดน้ำมัน' on cars, vans, pickups and wrecks, needing a hose (recipe from pvcpipe), fills a jerrycan; litres come from the prop's seed, and the state lives in WorldState. (c) 'ค้นท้ายรถ' on cars and taxis, with a small 'car' loot table (tape, bottle, tyre iron as a weapon, junk). Runtime and WorldState only, no GEN bump.

findings.title: Spawn rate and zombie cap don't scale with players or groups
findings.observation: One server-wide spawn_timer adds one zombie every 5 s by day (1.5 s at night), for a random player (main.gd:607-616). With 20 players spread out, each gets a new zombie about every 100 s. The 'near' cap is counted around the chosen player (survival.gd:458-463), so 5 friends standing together share the same 40 zombies a solo player faces. Only the server-wide ceiling scales with players (main.gd:610).
findings.why: The game is about co-op: a group should face more, not the same threat split five ways. And with 20-50 players, streets stay empty after one clearing, whatever the density tables say.
findings.suggestion: Give each player their own spawn timer (a peer → timer dictionary, main.gd:607). Set the local cap to MAX_ZOMBIES × (1 + 0.35 × other players within NEAR), still under the measured on-screen budget. With S1, draw from the block's pop so groups use a place up faster.

findings.title: Every home is the same, and you can't see what a building offers
findings.observation: Shophouses share the same tank size, a stove with 2-6 gas, and similar doors and windows; generators exist only in big buildings (things.gd:448-449). The player can't see the tank level (the tap's title is just 'ก๊อกน้ำ': things.gd:152-153), how much gas is left, or which opening stops the home counting as safe. Sleeping only says 'ประตูหน้าต่างยังเปิดอยู่' (doors or windows still open: survival.gd:136-137). Barred windows (เหล็กดัด) are drawn on facades (10_shophouse_e), but every window behaves the same (world.gd:17-19, doors.gd:105-113).
findings.evidence: things.gd:147-168, 448-449; survival.gd:89-104, 133-139; world.gd:17-19; doors.gd:98-113; 10_shophouse_e, 18_shop_inside_wide (barred upper windows)
findings.why: Home claiming (spray paint) is only a decision if homes differ and the differences can be read. Real Thai shophouses differ in exactly these security details.
findings.suggestion: (a) An on-demand readout, not on the HUD (the user wants a clean HUD): shown when you set your bed ('ตั้งเป็นเตียงประจำ') or through a 'ดูสภาพบ้าน' action on the stairs. It lists openings shut X/Y and highlights the open or broken one, tank %, gas uses left, water in the jar, and 'sounds from inside' when trapped > 0. (b) Vary homes with Thai features taken from rec.seed at runtime (no new random draws): ground-floor window grilles on ~40% (the glass can break, but neither zombies nor players climb through: a `barred` check where windows turn walkable), a collapsible steel gate (ประตูเหล็กยืด) on some fronts (see-through, strong, loud), a bigger or smaller tank, a spare gas bottle under the sink.

findings.title: Horde night ignores homes, noise and light
findings.observation: Horde zombies appear 280-420 px from a random living player and head straight at them (survival.gd:389-400): up to 160, one every 0.35 s (main.gd:610-613). Where you are doesn't matter. A lit building with a running generator, a dark boarded shophouse and an open street all get the same wave. ROADMAP wants hordes to go for occupied homes (ROADMAP.md:343).
findings.why: A horde that comes from the city and is drawn by what players do (noise, light, a generator) makes home choice and quiet habits pay off. It turns the biggest event into a decision rather than an arena.
findings.suggestion: Spawn the horde at the zone's edges and exits and along the avenues (w.exits, w.roads). Give it targets: the hottest noise-heat cells (S1), powered buildings (w.powered) and claimed beds. It sweeps in as a slow wave over several minutes, so a dark, quiet home can let it pass while a running generator becomes a beacon. Put its schedule on the season or real-time clock instead of every 3 game days (every 12 real minutes).

findings.title: Online world state grows without limit and every joiner gets all of it
findings.observation: send_world sends every door in the zone (changed or not), every searched container id and every pickup ever dropped (net.gd:106-122). Ground items never expire (save_game.gd:105-107). The WebSocket buffer already had to go to 4 MB because the world sent on joining passed 64 KB (ROADMAP.md:251). world_state.gd:9-10 notes that doors, containers and pickups still use their own older sync instead of WorldState.
findings.why: With 20-50 players searching everything and dropping junk all season, the join time, the save file and the first-frame hitch on web and mobile all keep growing.
findings.suggestion: Move doors and 'searched' into WorldState, so only changes from the generated city are stored and sent. Send pickups per nearby chunk instead of all at once. Let ground junk outside claimed homes decay after N real hours, keeping valuables and anything a player dropped deliberately for longer. This fits the 'core 10' rule already in ROADMAP.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed: spawn ring 320..840 px (survival.gd:465, NEAR-60), 300 px player guard (469-472), cap 40 free zombies within NEAR=900 (survival.gd:458-463, main.gd:12-13), drop beyond 1350 px (483-498), timer 5 s day / 1.5 s night (main.gd:610-616), idle 60% still (zombie.gd:78-80, 220-223), sight 120/55 (zombie.gd:71-72), stimulus reaches only existing zombies (main.gd:677-684). daily_hunt text 'ยิ่งแถวบ้านเงียบ คืนนี้ยิ่งหลับสบาย' (quests.cfg daily_hunt). 11_play_zoom: street empty. WRONG detail: 'every noise except the whistle is shorter than 320 px' - car alarm is 380 px every second for 14 s (actions.gd:61-63, 90), guns 650/850 (items.cfg:2061, 2083, not placed yet), bike engines 180-240 continuous (vehicles.cfg:24-94), thrown bottle 200 (combat.gd:60). Also missed: zombies.size() in the global cap counts trapped big-building zombies (main.gd:610), so near a compound street spawns stop entirely.
verdicts.reason: Core diagnosis is right and is the biggest systems cause of 'walk around, bored': density ignores place and kills refill in ~50 s. ROADMAP already lists '[ ] ความหนาแน่นซอมบี้/ของตามโซน' (310), the tension director with noise accumulating in one trip (391) and 'ภัยเพิ่มตามจำนวนคนและเสียง' (302). But the noise-range claim is overstated, and per-block pop is too coarse: victory.cfg blocks are huge (the SW shophouse block is 191x87 cells, the military hospital 191x127), so one player's kills would barely dent a block number and 'clear the soi round your home' would not be felt.
verdicts.revised_observation: Outside big buildings every zombie is spawned 320-840 px from a random living player until 40 free zombies are within 900 px (survival.gd:453-475); there is no place factor, and kills refill at 1 per 5 s (day) / 1.5 s (night) (main.gd:610-616). Noise only redirects zombies that already exist (main.gd:677-684). Most everyday noises (walk 45, run 115, hit 130, break 170, generator 190) are shorter than the spawn ring; car alarms (380) and whistles (300) reach past it, and guns (650/850) will when placed. Trapped big-building zombies count toward the global cap (main.gd:610), so beside a compound no street zombies spawn at all.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Do it in three steps, each playable. (1) S, data: add "density" per block in data/zones/victory.cfg (market 1.5, mall 1.3, avenues/roundabout 1.2, shophouses 0.8, hospital lawns 1.0); in _spawn_zombie reject a candidate cell with chance 1 - density/1.5, and skip cells inside buildings (see S7). (2) M: a population per 16-cell chunk (World.CHUNK), not per block: WorldState kind "chunk" {pop, pop_at}, start = density x ~3; spawn only where pop > 0, a kill in that chunk does pop-1, regrowth worked out from the clock like Buildings.tank (e.g. +1 per 20 real minutes). This makes clearing the streets around your home last. (3) M: noise heat: stimulus() adds radius/100 to a per-chunk heat dict that decays each minute; _spawn_zombie biases toward hot chunks and calls z.sense(pos). Count only free zombies (z.home < 0) in the global cap at main.gd:610. Keep the measured 40-60 on-screen ceiling. Runtime only, no GEN bump.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed: water/mama/fishcan places store, food, home (items.cfg ~276, ~288, ~332); home fallback (items.gd:703-710) and home counted as 'sold' at full weight (items.gd:668); antibiotic places=["med"] uncommon (items.cfg ~263-271); guns/ammo have no places ON PURPOSE (items.cfg:2044-2045 comment: waiting for the police station; ROADMAP:52, 209); military_hospital = [hospital, flats, hospital, office] (city_gen.gd:634-640); checkpoint is sandbags + army truck street_prop, not searchable (city_gen.gd:1141-1163). WRONG in the suggestion: syringe is ALREADY hospital-only (items.cfg syringe places=["hospital"], cure 100, rare). Missed: hospitals never give antibiotics, bandages, painkillers or first-aid kits: every 'med' room (ward, pharmacy, nurse, store: big_plans.gd:24) becomes place 'hospital' (items.gd:136-137), whose medicine list is only saline, splint, gauze, syringe. 00_zone_map: NW and NE compounds are near-identical grids.
verdicts.reason: Right lever and mostly data. ROADMAP itself names the problem ('ของมีทุกบ้าน', 385) and the ladder บ้านแถว < ห้าง/ตลาด < โรงพยาบาล < ฐานทหาร (324). The camp-location cost is a genuinely useful catch: the next agreed task is the refugee camp 'ในวัด' (ROADMAP:378) and victory.cfg has no wat block. The GEN bump can be avoided: army loot can be chosen at search time from the block's use.
verdicts.revised_observation: Food and water roll at full weight in every home kitchen and bedroom (items.gd:668, 703-710). Hospital rooms never give antibiotics, bandages, painkillers or first-aid kits: every 'med' room becomes place 'hospital' (items.gd:136-137), and that table holds only saline, splint, gauze and a rare syringe. So the safest pharmacy shophouse (0 trapped zombies) is the best place to cure a bite. The military hospital block is built from the same plans and tables as the civilian hospital and office blocks. Guns are held back on purpose for the planned police station.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: All runtime/data, no GEN bump. (a) items.cfg: add "hospital" to places of antibiotic (and make it rare in "med"), bandage, painkiller, firstaid. (b) Items.PLACE_BIAS: add home = {food = 0.6, drink = 0.6} and an EMPTY-by-place table (med 0.5, store 0.45, hospital 0.1) read in Items.roll. (c) Army loot without new containers: in Inventory._tick_search, when the building sits in a block with use military_hospital, send 'store'/'plant' rooms to a new 'army' place (ammo9/shells uncommon, pistol rare, stab vest, ration, batteries), and give its zombies DRESS 'army' through Items.zombie_place. Guns here are a user call, since ROADMAP keeps them for the police station. Make the checkpoint truck searchable as a one-shot street-prop action stored in WorldState (same mechanism as S9). (d) Decide now where the refugee camp goes in victory.cfg: a small wat block, or the military hospital lawn run by the army.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed: DAY_LENGTH 240 (main.gd:10); the clock runs whether or not anyone is online (main.gd:552-557), so ~360 game days per real day; horde every 3 game days = 12 real min (survival.gd:24, 371-373); street lamps skip the power check (world.gd:494-499 only skips room bulbs); powered only via generator runs (buildings.gd:100-108); tanks only by rain/pump (buildings.gd:69-94); loot 'made' = now minus 0-50% of life (inventory.gd:599-601); intro desc 'วันที่สามหลังเชื้อระบาด ไฟยังติด น้ำยังไหล' (quests.cfg:30) contradicts no power/mains; 11_play_zoom shows 'วันที่ 1'. ROADMAP:390 plans exactly this arc; ROADMAP:220 'ความยากเพิ่มตามวัน'; 345 season reset; 293 'รอดมา 34 วัน' as a stat.
verdicts.reason: Correct and important for the online season, but it is already planned. The analyst's real addition is that it needs a clock other than the 4-minute day, which is right. Simpler than 'seconds with a player on': the real (Unix) time since the season started, saved once in world.save, is easy to reason about and matches the 2-3 month reset. One fix is cheap now: the intro quest text says the power and water still work.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) S, now: rewrite quests.cfg intro_supplies desc so it matches the systems (e.g. 'ไฟดับ น้ำประปาไม่ไหลแล้ว'). (2) M: add season_start (unix time) to world.save (default = now for old saves) and a small data/eras.cfg of stages by real days since then: grid on (Buildings.powered true, street lamps lit), mains on (taps refill), then grid off, water off, thinner shelves (extra empty chance in Items.roll), more fakers. Readers use the same 'worked out when asked' pattern. Announce each stage through the existing fx_announce and radios. Show the survivor's own days alive in the HUD, not the server day. No GEN bump.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed: loot rolled once at search (inventory.gd:589-613), searched ids saved forever (save_game.gd:95-104) and sent to every joiner (net.gd:106-122); trapped only decreases (survival.gd:579-584); hunger 1200 s / thirst 720 s awake (survival.gd:13-14), which works out to ~7.5 noodles (40) and ~11 bottles (45) per real hour. Prefab rows hold 11-17 containers per shophouse (count of container letters in data/prefabs/*.txt), 00_zone_map shows ~45 big buildings, and every supermarket shelf cell is its own container (big_plans.gd:313-322, city_gen.gd:579-601). ROADMAP:406 marks budget restock '(ต้องมีก่อนเปิดออนไลน์)'; 366, 392 agree.
verdicts.reason: Numbers hold up (order of magnitude). Already planned and marked as required before going online. The suggestion is concrete and save-compatible with a VERSION migration. Two notes: it is not felt in solo play today, so it ranks below S1/S2/S5 for 'how the city feels now'; and it should be built together with S13, because it changes the same 'searched' data.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: As proposed (searched_at instead of a bool, a per-zone restock budget in containers with no player near and not in a claimed home, late restocks leaning to junk/canned food). Store searched_at in WorldState (kind "container") instead of the old list, so the S13 migration happens at the same time. Cheapest part first: raise the empty chance for 'store' shelves inside malls (Items.EMPTY by place) to ~0.7.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed: objective kinds (quests.gd:51-52) have no place; note() filters only kind/item (quests.gd:93-110); search reports nothing about place (inventory.gd:591); dailies are kill/search/cook/board anywhere (quests.cfg:72-126); map legend hardcodes วัด and คอนโด and colours only temple/chedi/sala/condo/store, so big buildings are plain brown (city_map.gd:40-41, 241-242); no road/block names drawn although victory.cfg:11-19, 39-48 has them. Missed: dailies are replaced every GAME day = every 4 real minutes (quests.gd:199-213), so any quest that sends you across the zone (6400 px at 55 px/s, player.gd:6 = ~2 min one way) would be wiped before you finish.
verdicts.reason: Good, cheap, and it pairs with S2's gradient. ROADMAP:380 already plans clue-by-place for the main story (ร้านยา → โรงพยาบาล → BTS). It only works once dailies stop resetting every 4 minutes (see the missed item).
verdicts.revised_suggestion: First make dailies last a real period (see missed item X1). Then: pass {block = block name, place = Items.place_in result} from inventory.gd:591 and from kills; add optional 'place'/'block' filters in Quests.note (two more 'continue' checks); add kinds 'visit' (enter a named block, checked in server_tick), 'power' (Things._do_generator_start) and 'fill' (canal scoop / tap), each one line in the kinds list plus one note() call. Add a few rows to quests.cfg that name places. On the M map, draw road names at the middle of each w.roads rect and block names at each w.blocks rect centre; colour big buildings by kind; build the legend only from kinds present in the zone.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed: rec.open 50% (city_gen.gd:375), shutter all up or down, 15% pried (city_gen.gd:529-540); shutter 150 hp (world.gd:18), opening noise NOISE_HIT (doors.gd:159); loot ignores the building (items.gd:655-656); trapped_start returns 0 for non-big (buildings.gd:43-44) and _tick_trapped skips non-big (survival.gd:520); GRAFFITI list incl. 'อย่าเข้า', 'ติดเชื้อ', 'ไม่มีของแล้ว', 'หนีไปวัด' and X-marks with random digits (building_prop.gd:34, 416-429). 10_shophouse_e: orange X on the คลินิก's closed shutter. Note: 'หนีไปวัด' points to a wat that this zone doesn't have.
verdicts.reason: Strong, low-art idea that makes the ~200+ shophouses differ and reads at play zoom. ROADMAP has the pieces (ซอมบี้ติดในตึก done for big buildings, 'ทุบประตูจากข้างใน' 89, 'บ้านที่ถูกปิดตาย' 303). Risk not addressed: _let_out fires at NEAR = 900 px from the building (survival.gd:531), so dozens of shophouse families would be out at once around a player, on top of the 40 roaming zombies (see missed item X3). S7 should land first, or the random in-house spawns muddle the signal.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: As proposed (Buildings.story(rec) from rec.seed/rec.open, no new random draws; 1-3 trapped in ~30% of shutter-down shophouses; empty chance x0.4 behind a shut shutter, x2 in open fronts; graffiti and X-mark numbers from the facts). Also: let shophouse families out only within ~250 px (not NEAR), because they are behind a shutter and only matter when you are at the door. Keep them idle until they hear something; then they bash the shutter from inside (the door-bash code path already exists). Replace 'หนีไปวัด' in GRAFFITI with a place this zone has (or keep it only in zones with a wat). Runtime + drawing only, no GEN bump.
