review.summary: The zone pipeline has good foundations: text prefabs with a validator, BigPlans that reuse the same letters, a compact 58-line zone file, deterministic seeds guarded by a fingerprint test, and saves that keep old cities aside. The weak point is that a zone file can only say "roads, one roundabout, one vertical BTS, full-width canals, blocks with 5 uses". Everything that makes a place recognisable (the monument, skywalk, bus stops, a temple for the planned refugee camp, Pratunam's pier, the Airport Rail Link, Baiyoke) has to be written in GDScript: Victory needed about 500 lines of new code for its 58 lines of data. The generator also has hard-coded habits that fight realism. Measured on seed 11, 0 of 203 shop fronts open onto a named street and rows average 1.57 units. Saves are keyed by generation-order index under one global GEN, so any layout change resets every zone. That will not survive online home claiming. With today's tools, Pratunam would take about 1 day of layout arithmetic plus 1-2 weeks of feature code, and it would reset Victory's saves too. The highest-leverage changes: (1) authored places and props in the zone file, (2) a zonebook preview plus a validator, (3) per-zone automatic fingerprints instead of the manual GEN, (4) cell-keyed saves before home claiming, (5) per-block frontage and density parameters.
strengths: Prefab text format (data/prefabs/*.txt) is readable, well documented (README) and validated by CityGen.prefab_problems() (city_gen.gd:115-142); interiors read as real shophouses (17_shop_inside, 19_shop_upstairs: shop in front, kitchen and water jar at the back, bedrooms upstairs).

BigPlans emits the same letter grid as prefabs, so one builder (_build_plan, city_gen.gd:473-613) handles shophouses and 3-7 storey hospitals, malls and markets; test_big_buildings checks 125 generated plans for size, aligned stairs and reachability (tests/test_big_buildings.gd:19-51).

The zone file is compact and in Thai (victory.cfg is 58 lines), zones are separate maps with exits, 'todo' signs and per-zone saves (zones.gd, save_game.gd:7-8), which matches the 'more zones, not bigger zones' plan.

Save discipline is careful: format migrations step by step with .vN copies, .bak, never overwriting unreadable or newer saves, and old-generator cities moved aside rather than deleted (save_game.gd:143-153, 421-450).
Determinism is protected by a fingerprint test and by keeping late passes free of random draws (city_gen.gd:152-160, 1183-1207, 1262-1265).

Rendering is built for scale: ground chunks batched by MeshCanvas, props streamed per 16x16 chunk at 3 chunks a frame, the overhead split into pieces (world.gd:316-445, overhead.gd:1-47), and a perf budget test.
WorldState ('store only what differs from the start', world_state.gd) is the right base for making saves survive layout changes.

findings.title: No shop front in Victory faces a named street; the zone file cannot say which side of a block is its street frontage
findings.observation: Measured in memory (Victory, seed 11): all 203 shop/store front doors open onto a 3-cell soi and none onto a street pavement. I walked the line just past each pavement of every named road. 0 cells are building fronts on any of the 8 road segments. Ratchaprarop is lined by 112 cells of side walls, Ratchawithi east by 86 cells of shophouse backs, Thanon Yothi by 95 cells of backs and 110 cells of wall, and Phahon Yothin by 176 cells of open ground and 96 of wall. Causes: shophouse rows start at the top of a block, with a soi after every row (city_gen.gd:774-783). Fronts only ever face south (README: 'shop fronts face south'). Big buildings are set back 2-3 cells behind lawns or walls (city_gen.gd:653).
findings.evidence: city_gen.gd:760-783, 797-826, 651-705; data/zones/README.txt:3-4,32; data/zones/victory.cfg:37-38; 15_ratchaprarop (the ร้านทอง row shows its side wall to Ratchaprarop), 12_ratchawithi, 00_zone_map, 10_shophouse_e
findings.why: A Bangkok street reads as Bangkok because shop fronts, shutters, signs and carts line the pavement. Right now the busiest streets in the zone are lined by walls, backs and car parks. This is the single biggest gap between 'recognisable district' and 'generic grid', and every future zone inherits it.
findings.suggestion: Stage it. (1) S: add `front` to each block in the zone file ("south" by default, or the edge that faces a named road). In _shophouse_block, lay the row on that edge flush against the pavement, with no soi between the row and the street. For big blocks, put the front row's entrance and forecourt toward the named road. This gives real fronts along the north side of every east-west road. (2) M: north-facing rows, with the prefab rows mirrored vertically. The facade is hidden in 3/4 view, so show it with a sign board on the roof parapet plus the existing FRONTS dressing and carts on the north pavement. No new camera angle is needed. (3) README rule for future zones: rotate each zone so the main shopping streets run left-right on screen (Phetchaburi and Yaowarat already do). Up-down avenues get corner units and vertical projecting signs (ป้ายแนวตั้ง).

findings.title: Landmarks and places cannot be written in the zone file, and the next agreed feature (refugee camp spawn in a temple) needs one
findings.observation: A plan knows only roads, junctions, one `circle`, full-width `canals`, one `bts` and `blocks` whose `use` is one of 5 kinds or shophouses (city_gen.gd:166-225, 634-640). All landmarks are code keyed to the roundabout: _landmarks returns early without a `circle` and places the monument, 8 bus stops and the minivan stand (city_gen.gd:294-321); the skywalk ring is drawn only if a circle exists (overhead.gd:38), and it fades in main.gd:1326-1332. The temple exists only in the legacy random layout (_temple_block, city_gen.gd:357, 829-845). The Victory commit added 58 lines of data but about 500 lines of code (city_gen +255, street_prop +166, overhead +80). The spawn is a single cell (victory.cfg:8).
findings.evidence: scripts/city_gen.gd:166-225, 294-321, 357, 634-645; scripts/overhead.gd:38; scripts/main.gd:1320-1340; git show --stat e6e19e8; ROADMAP.md:378 (camp in a temple = every newcomer's spawn); data/zones/victory.cfg
findings.why: A zone is recognised by its landmarks: Pratunam has the Saen Saep pier, Baiyoke and the clothes market; Siam has its malls and the two BTS lines; Yaowarat has its gold shops and the Chinese shrine. If each one is code, zone design time is really programming time, and the refugee camp cannot be placed in Victory at all today.
findings.suggestion: Extend the [plan] with two lists. (a) `places=[{"kind": "temple_camp", "rect": [x,y,w,h], "name": "วัด...", "front": "south"}, {"kind": "police", ...}]`: laid out before the blocks. Block fillers skip cells a place covers, and each place kind is built by BigPlans or a prefab (a plain neighbourhood temple with a parody name, never a royal site). (b) `props=[{"kind": "monument", "at": [200,160]}, {"kind": "busstop", "at": [...]}, {"kind": "vanstand", "at": [...], "n": 5}]`, so _landmarks becomes a loop over data (keep the circle-derived ones as defaults so Victory stays the same). Add `spawn_place: "temple_camp"`. Future landmarks then cost one draw function plus one data row.

findings.title: No zone validator or preview: the only way to see a zone is to bump GEN, start a new game and walk around
findings.observation: Zones._load_plan copies keys without any check (zones.gd:40-48). A misspelled `use` silently becomes shophouses (city_gen.gd:217-220). A block overlapping a road overwrites it (w.fill in _big_block, city_gen.gd:683). Nothing checks that exits sit on a road at the map edge, that they are reachable from spawn, or that a road's width and name match the partner exit in the next zone. Block rects and junctions are hand arithmetic (victory.cfg:22, 39-48: e.g. 24 = canal 16 + 6 + 2 towpath). tests/lookbook.gd already renders a PNG sheet for clothes, and CityMap already rasterises a zone into an image (city_map.gd:37-47); the 00_zone_map shot came from it. Measured build: Victory CityGen.build about 600 ms and World.generate about 850 ms, so a headless preview of 3 seeds takes a few seconds.
findings.evidence: scripts/zones.gd:40-48; scripts/city_gen.gd:214-220, 683; data/zones/victory.cfg:22,39-48; tests/lookbook.gd:1-10; scripts/city_map.gd:37-47; scripts/admin.gd:174-200 (goto by building kind only)
findings.why: The user named zone design time as the real limiter. A 10-second render-and-report loop replaces a restart-and-walk loop of minutes per tweak and catches mistakes before they become GEN bumps.
findings.suggestion: Add tests/zonebook.gd, modelled on lookbook: `godot -s res://tests/zonebook.gd -- --zone=pratunam --seeds=3 --out=...`. It builds the zone headless and writes (1) a PNG using CityMap's colours, overlaid with block outlines plus use and name, road names, exits and their partners, spawn, junctions, frontage colours along roads (front/side/back, from P1), and big-building overhang boxes (P10); (2) a text report: build time in ms, buildings per kind, containers per loot table, shophouses per row, soi share. Add `Zones.plan_problems(plan)`, the counterpart of prefab_problems: unknown keys and uses, blocks overlapping road or pavement, exits not on a road cell at their edge or mismatched in width with the partner exit, road overlaps with no junction, spawn not on pavement, and every exit reachable from spawn. Call it from test_city. In-game: admin click-on-M-map teleport, plus a 'rebuild zone from file' key for the host.

findings.title: Saves point at generation-order indices: every GEN bump resets every zone, which will not work once homes are claimed online
findings.observation: The world save stores doors by id, and searched, stripped and box contents by container id (save_game.gd:92-104). WorldState is keyed by building id, and player.bed is a container index kept only if the seed matches (save_game.gd:235-236). These ids are array positions in build order, so any change upstream shifts them all. That is why any `gen` mismatch discards the whole city: move_to_new_city plus a new random seed (save_game.gd:138-153, main.gd:270-273, 462-464). Stored boxes carry no cell, so their contents cannot be matched to the new city afterwards. GEN has gone from 1 to 9 over the project's history (213 commits). ROADMAP already wants 'update the city without losing home items' (ROADMAP.md:346) and seasonal resets every 2-3 months (ROADMAP.md:345).
findings.evidence: scripts/save_game.gd:90-125, 128-153, 229-236; scripts/main.gd:258-273, 455-470; scripts/world_state.gd:1-10; ROADMAP.md:340-346; git log --oneline -- scripts/city_gen.gd
findings.why: Home claiming (spray paint, locked cupboards, stash) is the long-term hook of the online game. If any layout fix wipes every stash in every zone, the solo dev either stops fixing layout or players lose their homes.
findings.suggestion: (1) Now (S, bump the save VERSION, not GEN): store identity with each change, e.g. boxes[id] = {cell, storey, kind, items} and doors with their cell (already at index 6). An old save then describes itself. On load after a generator change, match by (cell, storey, kind); stashes that match nothing go to the planned camp locker instead of vanishing. (2) Key future claims and locks by zone plus building rect position (or plus room rect for flat units), never by index. (3) Policy once online: layout-changing generator work ships only at season resets. Between seasons, only changes that leave the fingerprint unchanged ship (enforced by P5).

findings.title: GEN is manual and global, and the fingerprint test covers only Victory with one seed (Pratunam's generator is unguarded; clients are not checked)
findings.observation: test_city generates seed 777 with no zone id, so World.generate picks Zones.first(), i.e. Victory (test_city.gd:7-11, 32; world.gd:95). Pratunam is built by _layout_sections, _temple_block, _condo_block and _park_block (city_gen.gd:326-369, 829-870), none of which any fingerprint covers. A change there passes every test while its saves load against a different city. In the other direction, one global GEN (save_game.gd:138) means editing a future pratunam.cfg or its blocks resets Victory's saves too. Every client builds the city from the seed, but the join check compares only PROTOCOL (net.gd:13, 44). A client with a stale prefab or zone file therefore builds a different city (invisible walls, wrong container ids) with no warning.
findings.why: Forgetting a GEN bump corrupts saves silently, and a needless bump destroys every zone's saves. With 5+ zones and data files that change often, a manual global counter will fail sooner or later.
findings.suggestion: Move test_city's _fingerprint into CityGen.fingerprint(w): a hash of tiles, doors, containers, buildings and things (a few ms). Store it in world.save at save time. On load, regenerate from the seed and compare; a mismatch is 'oldcity' for that zone only, so no manual GEN bump is needed. Send the fingerprint in the join handshake so a client whose city differs is turned away with 'update the game'. Make test_city loop over every non-todo zone with 2 seeds, each with its own expected fingerprint table.

findings.title: Shophouse blocks are a hard-coded lattice: 1.57 houses per row, 28% of the map is soi, and block density cannot be set per block
findings.observation: _shophouse_block cuts a north-south soi every 12-16 cells (city_gen.gd:762-766), which leaves 9-13-cell segments. That fits only 1-2 units 6-7 wide. After every row of 13-15 cells it adds a 3-cell soi (776-783). There is a 7% chance of a walkway (807) and 10% of a minimart (813). Measured, Victory seed 11: 203 shophouses in 129 rows, 57 of them a single detached unit; mean 1.57 per row (Pratunam 1.81). Soi tiles cover 36,396 cells, 28% of the map. None of these numbers can be changed from the zone file: a block has only rect, use and name.
findings.evidence: scripts/city_gen.gd:760-826; data/zones/victory.cfg:39-48; 00_zone_map (lower-left and right blocks: a checkerboard of 1-2 unit boxes); 10_shophouse_e (units standing alone with 3-5 cell alleys each side); 09_shophouse_sw
findings.why: Real Bangkok rows run 10-30 units along a street, with a soi every 50-150 m. The current lattice is a maze of identical alleys: hard to navigate, no sense of 'main street vs back soi', and every house is a corner unit. It is also what the player sees most at play zoom.
findings.suggestion: Make the fillers parameterised, with block keys that default to today's values: `soi_every: [40, 70]` (perpendicular sois), `row_units: [8, 20]`, `back_soi: true/false` (rows back to back with no soi between them, as real ones are), `store_share`, `walkway`, `floors: [2, 4]`, `vacant`, and `trades: {"ร้านขายยา": 2, ...}` weights (see P8). Lay long rows along the frontage (P1) and let sois run perpendicular. The P3 report shows units per row and soi share so density can be tuned per district (Pratunam and Yaowarat dense, Din Daeng flats sparse).

findings.title: Street and block names are authored but never shown to the player
findings.observation: Every road in victory.cfg has a Thai name, stored in w.roads (city_gen.gd:190), but nothing reads it back: no street-name signs, and the M map shows only the zone name and exits (city_map.gd:207, 217). A search for ถนน or ซอย in scripts finds no signage. Block names appear only on hospital and market signs (city_gen.gd:698-702). Quests have no 'go to a place' objective (data/quests.cfg:8).
findings.why: A district feels recognisable when you can say 'I'm on Phaya Thai near Soi Rang Nam'. It also gives co-op players shared words for places, and gives quests and the camp's daily jobs something to point at. The data is already there.
findings.suggestion: (1) Print road names along each road rect on the M map, and block or place names at block centres. (2) Add blue Bangkok street-name signs (ป้ายชื่อถนน) at junction corners and soi mouths as street_props, placed in a pass at the very end of build with no random draws (like _zone_exits), so no GEN bump. (3) Add a quest objective `{"do": "reach", "place": "<block or place name>"}` once places exist (P2).

findings.title: Trades and building kinds are spread over about 6 files of hard-coded tables, including Victory-only names in CityGen
findings.observation: A shop trade lives in SIGNS, SIGN_LOOT and FRONTS (city_gen.gd:30-50, 1169-1180), TRADE_AWNING and TALL_SIGNS (building_prop.gd:30-33), and each prefab's `signs:` header. A big-building kind lives in BigPlans.KINDS, ROOM_W and TABLES plus furnish code (big_plans.gd:14-26), BLOCK_USES and SIGN_NAMES plus string tests like use.ends_with("hospital") (city_gen.gd:634-705), three `match data.kind` blocks in BuildingProp (building_prop.gd:43-58, 138-148, 587-631, 690-742), Items (items.gd:56-59, 133-145, 217-220, 372, 457-465) and zombie.gd:588. SIGN_NAMES hard-codes Victory names (ชัยพลาซ่า, อาคารพหลฯ ทาวเวอร์, คอนโด ราชวิถี, city_gen.gd:641-645), which would show up on a mall in Pratunam or Siam. city_gen.gd (1,287 lines) mixes prefab loading, plan layout, the legacy random layout, blocks, dressing and sizing. The old base-building code is still in world.gd:976-998 (chop, place_wall, hit_wall, wood).
findings.why: Phase 3 wants a police station, school and gas station, and each district needs its own trade mix. Today each of those means editing about 6 files, which is slow and error-prone for a solo beginner. It also breaks the project's own rule that new things should be data rows (ROADMAP.md:295).
findings.suggestion: Add data/trades.cfg with one section per trade: sign text, loot place, fronts, awning colour, tall_sign, default weight. Add data/places.cfg with one section per building kind: size and storey ranges, sign name pool, loot place, zombie place, facade style, trapped zombie range, and the furnish routine to use. Put per-zone name pools and trade weights in the zone file, e.g. `names: {mall: [...]}` for parody mall names per district. Keep only the drawing functions (facade styles) and furnish routines in code, looked up by name. Split city_gen.gd into prefabs, zone layout, block fillers and dressing. Retire _layout_sections once Pratunam is hand-drawn, and delete the dead base-building code.

findings.title: Zone geometry is limited to straight axis-aligned pieces, and junctions and block rects must be worked out by hand
findings.observation: Roads are axis-aligned rects (city_gen.gd:172-196). The skytrain is one line up a single column, with an optional half-circle round the roundabout (city_gen.gd:248-263). The legacy layout has a separate horizontal `bts_row` with its own draw and fade code (overhead.gd:24, main.gd:1334-1339). Canals always run the full width, horizontally (city_gen.gd:180-183). Junctions are listed by hand (victory.cfg:22). Blocks must be sized by hand to 'run right up to the pavements' (victory.cfg:34-48). Examples of what can't be written: the Airport Rail Link running across the map in Pratunam, two crossing BTS lines at Siam, a pier on Khlong Saen Saep, a canal that turns, the Din Daeng expressway, the curve of Yaowarat.
findings.why: Each missing primitive becomes one-off code for the zone that needs it (see P2). Hand-worked rects are where layout mistakes come from.
findings.suggestion: (1) One `overhead=[{"kind": "bts", "path": [[x,y], ...], "stations": [...]}, {"kind": "arl"}, {"kind": "skywalk"}]` list of polylines, drawn by one path-based Overhead function with one fade test in main.gd; retire bts_row. (2) Canals as a rect or path, with `piers`. (3) Derive junctions from road overlaps, and allow `blocks: "auto"`: the leftover cells between road plus pavement, cut into rects that the designer then labels with use and name. (4) Allow L-shaped roads made of axis-aligned segments. Do not attempt true diagonals: kerbs, lane paint, parked-vehicle orientation and sight rays all assume the axis grid. Squeeze and rotate districts as Victory did.

findings.title: Big-block layout ignores what the camera shows: tall buildings cover the row behind them, and the lawns are per-cell noise
findings.observation: A building's drawing reaches h pixels north of its footprint: h = 30 + (floors-1)*24 + 6 (building_prop.gd:7-8, 53-54). That is 132 px (8 cells) for a 5-storey hospital and 180 px (11 cells) for 7-storey flats. Rows are only 7-10 cells apart (city_gen.gd:679), and the top row sits 2-3 cells inside the block (653). So each row's roof covers the entrances and car park of the row behind it, and the north-edge rows cover the road or canal. Lawns are filled cell by cell (85% grass, 10% of those trees, the rest paved; city_gen.gd:693-694), which gives salt-and-pepper paving in the grass and dense woods.
findings.evidence: scripts/building_prop.gd:7-8, 43-58; scripts/city_gen.gd:653, 679, 684-694; 03_canal (the hospital block's front building drawn as a translucent slab over Khlong Sam Sen and its towpath); 06_office (the lower office's faded roof over the middle building's front); 04_mil_hospital, 05_hospital_block, 00_zone_map (speckled grounds)
findings.why: Entrances and landmarks hidden behind roofs make the big buildings hard to read and navigate. Speckled grounds look generated rather than like a Thai hospital compound (lawn, a few rain trees, car park lines).
findings.suggestion: In _big_block, space each row at least ceil(h_of_the_row_in_front / 16) + 2 cells from the row behind, and set the first row back from the block's north edge by its own height in cells. The P3 report flags any building whose overhang covers another building's door, a road or a canal. Replace the per-cell lawn with coherent patches (threshold a FastNoiseLite like world.tint, or whole lawn rects between driveways), trees in lines along walls and driveways, and car park bays painted in rows.

findings.title: One random stream runs through the whole build, so any change reshuffles everything after it
findings.observation: One RandomNumberGenerator runs through layout, blocks, buildings, street furniture, aftermath and Things (city_gen.gd:145-160, world.gd:104-106). The code works around this with repeated 'do this last, draw no random numbers' passes: _aftermath, Things.place_stoves, _size_vehicles, _size_beds, _shop_fronts, _zone_exits (city_gen.gd:152-160, 1183-1185, 1205-1207, 1221-1226, 1262-1265; things.gd:459-460). Two places already use their own seed: _shop_fronts (rec.seed*17+5, city_gen.gd:1191-1192) and _landmarks (city_seed+77, 313-314).
findings.why: Adding one building to the first block today changes every block after it. With per-block streams (plus cell-keyed saves, P4), a fix touches only the block it is in. That makes mid-season fixes possible and keeps the fingerprint diff meaningful.
findings.suggestion: With one final GEN bump, derive sub-seeds: block_seed = hash([city_seed, zone, block rect, use]); building interior = rec.seed (already drawn); separate streams for street furniture per road (hash of road rect), aftermath per junction, and Things per building. Pass these sub-RNGs to _shophouse_block, _big_block and so on instead of the shared rng. Then remove the 'must be last' ordering rules from comments and code.

findings.title: A zone costs about 125 MB and 850 ms to build, mostly display nodes (the server builds them too), because game state lives in the nodes
findings.observation: Measured headless on the dev PC for Victory seed 11: CityGen.build 589 ms, whole World.generate 838 ms, 31,131 streamed nodes (11,655 FurnitureProp, 7,844 decor, 2,421 doors, 2,935 street props, 1,214 things), 118k upstairs cells in Dictionaries. Static memory: layout data alone +33 MB, whole world +125 MB. The Pratunam placeholder: 250 ms / 360 ms / 51 MB. Every client builds this, and so does every zone switch, on the main thread (main.gd:455-470). A dedicated server builds all 31k draw nodes it never renders (world.gd:128). It cannot skip them, because container state lives in the nodes: save_game.gd:98-104 reads FurnitureProp.items and .searched. WorldState notes that doors and containers are not yet moved in (world_state.gd:9-10).
findings.evidence: Measured with a scratch probe (CityGen.build / World.generate timing, Performance.OBJECT_COUNT, OS.get_static_memory_usage); scripts/world.gd:94-128, 131-252; scripts/save_game.gd:98-104, 170-185; scripts/world_state.gd:9-10; scripts/main.gd:455-470; ROADMAP.md:309, 412
findings.why: ROADMAP plans to measure memory per zone on mobile and to run several zone servers per machine. Web wasm is typically 2-4x slower than desktop, so a zone switch could stall for several seconds, and 125 MB per zone limits how many zones fit on one machine and whether it runs on a phone. Measure on the web first, per the perf rules.
findings.suggestion: (1) Measure the zone switch on the web build with F3 and a timer around _make_world. (2) Move container state (items, searched, stripped) and doors into WorldState, as ROADMAP core 10 already plans. (3) Then create prop nodes lazily when a chunk first streams in (World._attach), and never on a dedicated server; memory should drop to about the 33 MB of layout data. (4) Only if profiling points there: _size_beds rebuilds w.decor with filter() for each bed (city_gen.gd:1258), and _bike_near scans every street prop for each bike (city_gen.gd:1096-1101).

findings.title: Prefabs stop at floor 2, but shophouses are given 2-3 storeys; there is no prefab preview and no per-zone prefab set
findings.observation: The loader recognises only 'floor 2:' (city_gen.gd:100-109: storeys = [upper]). add_building gives shops floors 2-3 (city_gen.gd:378), so about half the facades show a third storey you can never enter: the stairs go from floor 2 straight to the roof (README line 36). _build_plan already loops over any number of storeys (city_gen.gd:611-613). The 13 prefabs are shared by every zone; nothing lets Pratunam favour clothes-wholesale shophouses and guesthouses, or Yaowarat gold shops and Chinese pharmacies. There is no visual sheet of the prefabs, only the text and the letter validator.
findings.why: Realism-first: Bangkok shophouses are 3-4 storeys with the family upstairs, and a facade that promises a floor that does not exist breaks trust. District-specific prefabs are the cheapest way to make zones feel different, because they are data.
findings.suggestion: Accept 'floor 3:' and 'floor 4:' in the loader (same rows and ~ rows, stairs in the same place; extend prefab_problems accordingly). Set rec.floors from the plan's floor count, or cap the facade at it. Add an optional `zones: pratunam, yaowarat` header plus per-zone trade weights (P8). Add tests/prefabbook.gd, a PNG of every prefab at widths 6 and 7 and depths 13 and 15, every floor, drawn with the real furniture props, like lookbook.

findings.title: A tracing importer (PNG or OpenStreetMap to draft zone file) would cut the hand arithmetic
findings.observation: victory.cfg was written by hand from OpenStreetMap, squeezed about 2.5x and rotated (victory.cfg:1-4). Every road, block, junction and exit rect is typed as numbers, and blocks must line up exactly with pavement edges (victory.cfg:34-38). No tool in the repo reads a map, and the zone README describes only hand drawing.
findings.evidence: data/zones/victory.cfg:1-58; data/zones/README.txt:1-35; ROADMAP.md:313, 411-415 (3-5 Bangkok districts, then provinces)
findings.why: With 5 Bangkok zones planned and provinces after, typing rects from an OSM screenshot is the slowest and most error-prone step. A tracer turns an evening of arithmetic into about 20 minutes of painting.
findings.suggestion: Add tools/trace_zone.gd (headless). Input: a 400x320 PNG painted over a scaled OSM screenshot in any paint program, with a fixed palette (road, median, pavement, canal, one colour per block use, single-pixel markers for spawn, exits, places and props). Output: a draft data/zones/<id>.cfg with road rects (merged runs), medians, junctions, canals, block rects with `use`, and marked places. The designer then only adds names. The PNG is an authoring source, not game art, so the runtime stays text-only. Run zonebook (P3) on the result straight away. OSM Overpass JSON import is a possible later step; the PNG path is simpler for a solo dev.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed in code. prefab_problems requires the bottom row to hold D/U (city_gen.gd:125), so every shophouse faces south. _shophouse_block lays rows from the block's top edge with a 3-cell soi after each one (city_gen.gd:774-783). In victory.cfg the two shophouse blocks touch named roads only with their NORTH edge (backs to Thanon Yothi and Ratchawithi east) or their west edge (side walls on Ratchaprarop). Their south edge is the map-edge pavement. In 15_ratchaprarop the west end of the ร้านทอง row sits on the pavement while its front faces the soi. Every block whose SOUTH edge meets a named E-W road (military_hospital, hospital, office, mall) is a big-building compound set back 2-3 cells (city_gen.gd:653). So '0 fronts on a named street' matches the code (I did not recount it). BuildingProp draws only the south face (building_prop.gd:3-5, 59), so a road running up and down can never show shop fronts.
verdicts.reason: The diagnosis is right and this is the biggest realism gap. The suggestion is off in two ways. Stage (1) as written changes nothing in Victory: no shophouse block has a named road on its south edge, and 'fronts on the north side of E-W roads' can only come from carving shophouses out of the big blocks. Stage (2), north-facing rows, fights the fixed camera: their front wall is never drawn, and the pavement in front of them sits under their own roof overhang.
verdicts.revised_observation: All shophouse fronts face south onto a soi or onto the map-edge pavement. Victory's shophouse blocks meet named roads only with their backs (Thanon Yothi, Ratchawithi east) or their side walls (Ratchaprarop). Every block whose south edge meets a named E-W road is a big-building compound set back 2-3 cells.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) Data first. In victory.cfg, split a 15-cell-deep 'shophouses' block off the south edge of each block where the real street is lined with shops (check OSM). Example: office/condo block -> [209,24,191,112] office + [209,136,191,15] shophouses along Ratchawithi east. (2) In _shophouse_block, lay rows from the block's south edge upward, so the last row's shutters sit on the pavement and any leftover vacant lot ends up at the back. (3) Add a soi_every key (P6) so the strip becomes one long row, not 1-2-unit pieces. (4) Do not make north-facing rows. On the south side of E-W roads, dress the backs instead. (5) README rule for new zones: rotate them so the shopping streets run left-right. Roads running up and down get corner units, tall signs and carts. One GEN bump, shared with P6/P10/M3.

verdicts.fact_check: Plan keys confirmed as only roads, junctions, circle, canals, bts, blocks, exits and spawn (city_gen.gd:166-225). _landmarks returns early without a circle, and otherwise places the monument, 8 bus stops and the van stand (city_gen.gd:294-321). The skywalk is drawn only when a circle exists (overhead.gd:38). _temple_block is called only from _layout_sections (city_gen.gd:357). More hard-codes: the station board text 'อนุสาวรีย์ชัยสมรภูมิ' (overhead.gd:116), and any zone with a roundabout would get Victory's monument. ROADMAP:378 says the camp in a temple is every newcomer's spawn. Victory's spawn [191,176] (victory.cfg:8) lies on the roundabout carriageway (distance 18 from centre, r=28), not on pavement as the README asks. The '500 lines for Victory' figure is overstated. Commit e6e19e8 added 633 lines to scripts, but most of it is the reusable plan interpreter (roads, medians, canals, bridges, exits, per-road furniture). Code that exists only for landmarks is about 150 lines: _landmarks ~28, _monument ~37, _busstop, _draw_skywalk ~20, _draw_station ~20.
verdicts.reason: This blocks the agreed next task (refugee camp spawn). But the cheapest way to unblock it is a new block use that calls existing code, not a new places/props system.
verdicts.revised_observation: The zone file cannot say 'a temple here': _temple_block exists but only the legacy random layout calls it. Landmarks are keyed to the roundabout, and the station name is hard-coded. The code that exists only for landmarks is about 150 lines. Most of the Victory commit is the generic plan interpreter.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) Now (S). In _layout_plan, add a 'temple' block use that calls the existing _temple_block. Carve a ~40x35 block in victory.cfg for a neighbourhood temple with a parody name (e.g. from the east shophouse block). Add spawn_block: "<name>" so new survivors start at the temple gate. GEN bump. (2) Put the station name into the plan (bts.station_name), and add a monument: true key on the circle, so another zone can have a roundabout without Victory's monument. (3) Wait on a generic props=[...] list until Pratunam needs its pier. At that point, turn _landmarks into a loop over data, with today's roundabout-based placements as defaults.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. _load_plan copies keys with no checks (zones.gd:40-48). An unknown use falls through to _shophouse_block (city_gen.gd:217-220). _big_block fills the whole rect with SOI (city_gen.gd:683), and soi columns are cut across the whole block (city_gen.gd:765), so a block that overlaps a road overwrites it. test_zones only checks two Victory exits by id. tests/lookbook.gd already writes a PNG sheet. CityMap builds an Image from the tiles (city_map.gd:37-47). admin req_goto only finds buildings by kind (admin.gd:172-197). Build timings not re-measured; they are plausible.
verdicts.reason: Fits 'zone design time is the real limiter'. It is mostly test-side code, with no generation or save risk.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Order by cost. (1) S: Zones.plan_problems(), called from test_city and test_zones. It should flag unknown keys and uses; blocks overlapping road or pavement; exits not on a ROAD cell at their edge; exit width different from the partner's (when the partner has a plan); spawn not on SIDEWALK or PLAZA (Victory's current spawn fails this); and any exit unreachable from spawn (reuse test_city's flood fill). (2) S-M: tests/zonebook.gd. It copies CityMap._colour, colours big buildings by kind, prints block, road and exit names, and writes a short text report. (3) Later: admin click-to-teleport on the M map. Skip the 'rebuild zone from file' key for now: Zones is loaded once at startup and clients also build the city.

verdicts.fact_check: Facts confirmed. Doors are saved with their cell (save_game.gd:94). searched, stripped and boxes are keyed by container index with no cell (save_game.gd:95-104). Any gen mismatch means 'oldcity', which calls move_to_new_city and starts a new random seed (save_game.gd:138-153, main.gd:268-273, 462-464). The bed index is kept only for the same seed (save_game.gd:235-236). GEN was bumped 8 times between 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-27 (git log -G 'const GEN'); 213 commits in total. But ROADMAP already covers the main risk. The claimed home and the locked-cupboard contents are stored per account in the database (ROADMAP:267). Wiped or abandoned homes' items go to the camp locker (ROADMAP:342, 346). Seasonal resets are planned (ROADMAP:345).
verdicts.reason: True, but nobody can claim a home and nothing runs online yet. A save-format change now pays little: with one RNG stream (P11), matching boxes by cell after a layout change would miss almost everything after the edit anyway.
verdicts.revised_observation: World-save ids are array indices, so any GEN bump resets the zone. Claimed homes and locked-cupboard contents are already planned to live in the account database and to fall back to the camp locker.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Do this together with home claiming, not now. Key a claim by (zone, building rect), never by building id. Keep locked-box contents with the claim in the player/account record (ROADMAP:267). On 'oldcity', move claimed contents to the camp locker (ROADMAP:346) instead of trying to match boxes. Add one policy line to ROADMAP: once online, generator work that changes the layout ships only at season resets.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. test_city builds seed 777 with no zone id (test_city.gd:7, 32), so it gets Zones.first() = victory (world.gd:95). Pratunam goes through _layout_sections, _temple_block, _condo_block and _park_block (city_gen.gd:148-149, 326-369), which no fingerprint covers. GEN is one global value (save_game.gd:138). The join check compares only PROTOCOL (net.gd:13, 44). However, PROTOCOL has been bumped together with GEN by habit (net.gd:13 comment: '22: big buildings (CityGen.GEN 9)'). So the stale-client gap only opens when a data file is edited without a bump.
verdicts.reason: Cheap, and it closes a silent-corruption path. Two cautions. First, the built-in hash() of Arrays is not guaranteed stable across Godot versions, so an engine upgrade could silently wipe every save. Second, a fully automatic 'oldcity' hides accidental drift instead of flagging it.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Keep GEN, and make it per zone (a gen key in each zone file) so editing Pratunam no longer resets Victory. Add CityGen.fingerprint(w) with a stable hash (HashingContext SHA-256 over var_to_bytes of cells and kinds, or a hand-written FNV loop) and store it in world.save. On load, if GEN matches but the fingerprint differs, print a loud error and treat only that zone as oldcity. Send the fingerprint in the hello rpc. Make test_city loop over every non-todo zone, each with its own expected fingerprint.

verdicts.fact_check: Code confirmed (city_gen.gd:762-783, 807, 813). I counted on 00_zone_map (3 px per cell): the two shophouse blocks hold 134 building rows, 7-14 cells wide, and 77 of them are 8 cells or narrower (one unit). That fits ~1.57 units per row. But '28% of the map is soi' is misattributed. I count ~36.5k soi-coloured cells inside blocks, and only ~13.2k of them are in the shophouse blocks. The other ~23k are big-block driveways and car parks (w.fill(b, World.SOI), city_gen.gd:683). Inside the shophouse blocks, sois and alleys take 40% of the land (6,592/16,617 and 6,577/16,576). 10_shophouse_e shows single units standing between alleys.
verdicts.reason: The lattice is real, and it is what the player sees most. But back_soi: false (rows back to back) makes half the rows face north, and this camera cannot show those fronts. Sois also need to be wider, not just fewer: a 3-cell soi is fully covered by the roof of the row south of it (see missed M3).
verdicts.revised_observation: Shophouse blocks are 40% soi and alley, with rows of 1-2 units. Across the whole map, most soi-type ground is actually big-block car parks, not shophouse alleys.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Add block keys that default to today's values: soi_every: [40, 70] for cross sois, front_soi: 5-6 (at least the roof overhang of the row south of it), row_depth, store_share, walkway, and trades weights. Keep every row facing south. Show units per row and soi share in the zonebook report. One GEN bump, shared with P1/P10/M3.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. Road and block names are stored (city_gen.gd:190, 216) and never read back; a grep finds no street-name labels in scripts. The M map draws only the zone name and exits (city_map.gd:207-217). Its legend is left over from the random layout: it lists วัด and คอนโด, which Victory does not have (city_map.gd:238). Every big building is drawn the same brown (city_map.gd:43-44), so on 00_zone_map the hospitals, malls, offices and market cannot be told apart. quests.cfg has no reach-a-place objective (data/quests.cfg:6-21).
verdicts.reason: The data already exists and the change is cheap. It gives co-op players shared names for places and supports the planned story chain ร้านยา -> โรงพยาบาล -> BTS (ROADMAP:380).
verdicts.revised_suggestion: As proposed, plus two things. Colour big buildings by kind on the M map and build the legend from what the zone actually contains. Add a reach/enter objective keyed by building kind or block name. Append the street signs to street_props after _landmarks, with no RNG draws; street_prop ids are array indices (world.gd:232-233), so appending at the end keeps existing ids and needs no GEN bump.

verdicts.fact_check: The tables are confirmed. SIGNS and SIGN_LOOT (city_gen.gd:30-50). FRONTS (city_gen.gd:1169-1180). TRADE_AWNING, TALL_SIGNS and SIGN_COLORS (building_prop.gd:26-33). BLOCK_USES, and SIGN_NAMES with Victory-only names (city_gen.gd:634-645). Items PLACES, place_in, zombie_place and ZOMBIE_PLACES (items.gd:56-59, 133-145, 372, 457-465), and zombie.gd:588. chop, place_wall, hit_wall and wood are dead code with no callers (world.gd:976-998). This does not change the fingerprint: the pick uses rec.seed % size, not the RNG. Delete the dead base-building code. verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. A building's drawing rises h px above its footprint's north edge (building_prop.gd:3-5, 53-54, 59, 72). Hospitals have 4-5 storeys (big_plans.gd:15), so they overhang 108-132 px (6.8-8.3 cells). Flats and offices have 5-7, so 132-180 px (8.3-11.3 cells). verdicts.reason: Solid and cheap. The GEN bump can be shared with P1/P6.

verdicts.fact_check: Confirmed. One rng runs through the whole build (world.gd:104-106, city_gen.gd:145-160). The 'last, draws nothing' passes are at city_gen.gd:152-160, 1183-1207, 1262-1265. verdicts.fact_check: Architecture confirmed. Every prop node is created in _spawn_props during generate (world.gd:131-252). Container state lives on FurnitureProp nodes (save_game.gd:98-104). Write 3rd floors for home, pharmacy and goldshop (ห้องพระ, drying room). The zones: header is cheap; the prefabbook is optional.

missed.title: Big-building blocks are packed to the edges: 45 big buildings, 10 of them hospitals
missed.observation:
_big_block keeps placing rows of buildings until the block is full, cycling through BLOCK_USES (city_gen.gd:651-679). Counted per block on 00_zone_map (seed 11):
- Military hospital block: 16 buildings in a 4x4 grid. The kinds cycle hospital/flats/hospital/office, so 8 are hospitals.
- Hospital block: 3 buildings, 2 of them hospitals.
- Office block: 20 buildings in a 4x5 grid (10 offices, 10 flats).
- Market block: 4 sheds. Plus 2 malls.
That makes 45 big 3-7-storey buildings, including 10 hospitals. Each one holds 2-14 trapped zombies (buildings.gd:37-46).
missed.evidence: city_gen.gd:634-640, 651-679; big_plans.gd:14-20; buildings.gd:37-46; 00_zone_map (top half: two regular grids of 16 and 20 same-sized rectangles)
missed.why: The top half of the zone looks like a business park, not a Bangkok district. It also makes the rare, dangerous destination common: the story chain ร้านยา -> โรงพยาบาล (ROADMAP:380) and the planned difficulty labels (ROADMAP:324) rely on hospitals being scarce. Ten hospitals' worth of medicine near the spawn weakens the 'reason to take a risk' the fun section says is missing (ROADMAP:385). Rough target for Victory: 2-3 hospital buildings in the military compound, 1-2 in the hospital block, about 6-8 offices and flats. Data plus about 5 lines of code; one GEN bump.

missed.title: Danger and loot are the same everywhere in a zone; the zone file cannot mark risky places
missed.observation: Street zombies spawn anywhere walkable, 320-840 px around a random player, capped at MAX_ZOMBIES = 40 per player (survival.gd:453-478, main.gd:12-13). Today a back soi, the monument and the military compound are equally dangerous on the street, so the map itself offers no risk-versus-reward choice, even though the loot tables already differ by place.
missed.suggestion: Add optional danger (zombie spawn weight and cap multiplier) and loot (multiplier on the empty chance) keys per block and per zone in the zone file. In _spawn_zombie, keep picking the candidate cell as now, but accept it with probability danger(block at that cell) / max_danger, and scale the per-player cap by the danger around the player. This is runtime only: no change to generation and no GEN bump. It can later drive the difficulty labels ROADMAP:324 wants.
