Real car sois are 4-8 m wide, so 5-6 cells is still realistic. This is the same rule P10 proposes for big blocks. One GEN bump, shared with P1/P6/P10.

review.summary: First impression (opinion): the code-drawn look is cohesive and moody, and it is more Thai than I expected. The shophouse facades, the back kitchens with a โอ่ง jar, the vendor umbrellas, the red-white kerbs and the sagging cables all look right, and the monument, skywalk ring and BTS curve are recognisable at wide zoom. The weak part is the city as a whole. It reads as a clean generated grid more than as Victory Monument three days after the outbreak: roads nearly empty, interiors tidy and fully stocked, big compounds that look like copies of each other, and almost nothing to steer by (no names, no street signs, no labels on the map). The default zoom 4 makes this worse, because half the frame is empty asphalt and a roof. My top picks, all mostly data-driven: open the street view up; fill the main roads with an evacuation jam; add outbreak vignettes; show ransacked/intact states that match the loot; give shops and streets real names.
strengths: Shophouse facades are the best thing in the game and read instantly as Bangkok: iron window grilles, boarded windows, striped awnings, vertical red Chinese plaques, Thai trade signs (ขายส่ง, คลินิก, ร้านทอง, มินิมาร์ท 24 ชม., โจ๊ก ข้าวต้ม), creeping vines, a barber pole and a spray-painted X on a closed shutter (10_shophouse_e, 15_ratchaprarop, 18_shop_inside_wide).

Shophouse interiors follow real Thai life: shop at the front, back kitchen with gas bottle and sink, a dragon-pattern โอ่ง, stairs marked '↑ ชั้น 2'. Upstairs has made beds, a standing fan, a chest of drawers and a shelf shrine, with '↑ ดาดฟ้า' to the roof (17_shop_inside, 19_shop_upstairs).

The street kit carries the setting: red-white kerbs, parasol vendor carts, motorbikes parked nose-out, lamp posts, sagging bundles of cables, water hyacinth on Khlong Sam Sen, a long-tail boat, a spirit house in the hospital grounds (02, 03, 04, 11, 12).

The landmark geometry is right. At zoom 1 (16_wide) the obelisk with five figures, the skywalk ring and the BTS curve read as Victory Monument, and the BTS curve beside the mall has convincing 3/4 depth (07_mall).
Time-of-day grading is strong and atmospheric without cluttering the HUD: evening sepia (14) and blue night with the player's light pool (13).

Interaction feedback is clear: a yellow outline on the usable fridge and floor-change labels in Thai (09, 17). Hospital upper-floor wards with beds, curtains and nurse stations read as a hospital (21).
The HUD at play zoom is compact: day/time, a single quest card, a status block and the hotbar (11_play_zoom).

findings.title: Default play zoom shows too little street and half of it is roof
findings.observation: Fact: at zoom 4 (11_play_zoom) the player stands at screen (605,340). Everything above is empty asphalt (y 0-300). Everything below is roof: a grey corrugated roof x0-385, a faded brown roof x577-897, a beige roof x897-1280. The pavement, two lamp posts, a tree and a vendor umbrella just south of the player show only through the brown fade, and the hotbar sits over part of it (x405-875, y632-695). That leaves about 5.5 m of world between the player and the top or bottom edge. At zoom 2.5 (09, 10, 17) the same kind of place reads as a scene: shop fronts, the soi, the interior and parked bikes all fit in one frame.
findings.why: Opinion: survival play depends on seeing a threat before it reaches you. 5.5 m vertically is about one second of a runner's approach, and roofs eat part of that. Walking around bored is also partly a framing problem: at zoom 4 a street is grey plus one roof, so the city's detail never reaches the screen. Project Zomboid and Darkwood show several rooms or a whole street corner by default.
findings.suggestion: Use zoom by context and keep zoom 4 for tight spaces. Street default about 2.5-3 (roughly 32x18 to 27x15 m at 1280x720), zoom 4 automatically inside buildings, about 2 on a vehicle, with a smooth 0.3 s blend. The player can still override with the wheel inside the 1-6 range. If zoom is currently a pixel scale, also fix the visible world size (for example about 30 m wide) so a 720p laptop and a 1440p monitor see the same area; in co-op a bigger screen should not see more. Cost: about 1.5-1.8x more zombies on screen. The roadmap says 40-60 dressed zombies still run smoothly, so measure with F3/?bench after the change.

findings.title: Bangkok's biggest bus hub has almost no stalled traffic; add an evacuation jam
findings.observation: Fact: in the roundabout frames the ring holds 1 sedan and 1 van (01_monument at (365,125) and (1215,480)). 16_wide shows 1 bus, 1 van with cart, 1 sedan and 1 burnt car. The 8-lane Ratchawithi (12) has 3 wrecks (flipped black car at (1190,130), tipped white van, grey van) plus 2 parked cars. The 14-cell Phahon Yothin under the BTS (02) has 5 vehicles. The asphalt between them is empty, marked only by small flecks.
findings.why: Opinion: a Thai player expects Victory Monument after an outbreak to be solid with buses, vans and motorbikes left by people who ran. This is the single strongest 'after the outbreak' image available. It also plays well: stalled cars give cover and chokepoints, the roadmap says every vehicle is climbable (escape over car roofs), and trunk/boot searching is already planned as loot. Right now the widest roads are the emptiest and most boring spaces in the zone.
findings.suggestion: Make it table-driven. Add optional keys to each road in data/zones/victory.cfg, for example {"jam": 0.7, "toward": "north"}, and to the circle, for example "jam": 0.8. The street-vehicle placement (likely in city_gen.gd / street_prop.gd) fills lanes with vehicles nose-to-tail pointing toward the exit, with small angle and offset noise. Add some open doors, a few buses at the stops with suitcases and bags on the tarmac, and a motorbike layer weaving between them. Keep 1-2 lanes passable so zombies and players can still path. Suggested densities: Phahon Yothin northbound and the ring about 0.8, Ratchawithi about 0.4, sois 0. Put the new random draws at the end of build, bump GEN and update the test_city fingerprint.

findings.title: No traces of the outbreak or evacuation at the places where they would be
findings.observation: Fact: the military hospital compound (04, 20) holds parked sedans, trees, bins and a spirit house at (922,600). There is no gate checkpoint, tent, sandbag, army truck or stretcher. The hospital front (05) has 2 cars, a red vending machine and a dense grove. The monument island (01, 14, 16) is a clean plaza with trees and statues. The only narrative marks I found in 22 shots are one spray-painted X on the คลินิก shutter (10, around (1128,185)), boarded windows, blood smears and overturned cars on Ratchawithi (12).
findings.evidence: 04_mil_hospital, 05_hospital_block, 20_hospital_ground, 01_monument, 16_wide, 10_shophouse_e; ROADMAP 'ข้อที่ยังไม่มีในแผน ... ร่องรอยเล่าเรื่อง'
findings.why: Opinion: places tell the story, and they also tell the player where to go and what to fear. A triage tent says 'medical loot, and probably infected'. A failed army checkpoint says 'weapons, but it fell'. In Zomboid and DayZ the loot goals come largely from these readable sites. The roadmap's fun section says the game lacks 'something I want' and 'a reason to take the risk', and vignettes provide both without new systems.
findings.suggestion: Add a small scene table, data/scenes.cfg. Each scene is a list of prop placements relative to an anchor, plus a loot bias and an optional zombie hint (fake corpse, guard with whistle). Example scenes: triage (3 tents, cots, IV poles, body-bag row), army_checkpoint (sandbags, barrier, army truck, spent casings), failed_evac_point (tents and supply crates on the monument plaza, a bus with open doors), barricaded_home (furniture against the shutter, spray message 'มีคนอยู่' — this teaches the home-claim language before the player gets the mechanic), looted_pharmacy. Place them by name in victory.cfg: "scenes": [{"kind": "army_checkpoint", "at": [190,88]}, {"kind": "triage", "at": [60,190]}, {"kind": "failed_evac_point", "at": [200,160]}]. Placement code reads the table (decor_prop.gd / city_gen.gd). New draws at the end, so bump GEN.

findings.title: Interiors look untouched; show ransacked, barricaded and intact states and tie them to loot
findings.observation: Fact: the pharmacy ground floor (17, 18) has both shelf rows (x450-705, y385-690 in 17) fully and neatly stocked. The upstairs beds are made and the drawers closed (19). The hospital wards have made beds in neat rows (21). The ground-floor rooms (20) are tidy with items against the walls. Nothing on the floors except the odd box. Nothing in these shots tells a searched container from an unsearched one. ROADMAP 'ของดรอป' says containers stay empty forever once searched and are first-come.
findings.why: Opinion: a pharmacy is the first place looted in an outbreak, so a full one breaks the fiction. The bigger issue is play: the core loop hinges on deciding whether to take a risk. If a ransacked shop has little loot and looks ransacked, and a locked shutter promises more but is noisy to force, the player decides from what they see. In co-op, visibly opened drawers and doors also say 'a teammate or a stranger was here'.
findings.suggestion: Give each building a state picked at build time (or derived from a hash of its cell, so the random stream is untouched): intact (shutter down, full shelves, better loot, noise to open), ransacked (shelves drawn at 30-50% fill, boxes and pills on the floor, broken glass at the front, lower loot multiplier), barricaded (furniture against doors, maybe a survivor note). Keep the numbers in a data table: state weights per trade/use and a loot multiplier read by items.cfg lookups. Separately, draw searched containers differently (drawer out, cabinet door ajar, fridge open) in furniture_prop.gd from the existing searched flag. That part is purely visual and needs no GEN bump.

findings.title: You cannot give directions: shops have only generic trade names, there are no street signs, and the map has no labels
findings.observation: Fact: every shop sign in the shots is a bare trade word: 'โจ๊ก ข้าวต้ม', 'ผัดไทย' (09), 'ขายส่ง', 'คลินิก' (10), 'ร้านทอง' (15 and 18), 'มินิมาร์ท 24 ชม.' (18). With 11 trades plus minimart they must repeat across the zone. No street-name or soi-number sign appears in any of the 22 shots. The M-map picture (00) has no text or icons. The monument is a plain grey disc at (600,480), and the BTS line, station and skywalk are not drawn. victory.cfg already names 8 road segments and 5 blocks (lines 12-19, 40-47).
findings.why: Opinion: sense of place in co-op means being able to say 'meet at ร้านทองเฮงเจริญ, second soi past the bus stop'. Named shops also make individual houses memorable, which home claiming later depends on. Generic signs make every block feel like the last.
findings.suggestion: (a) Add a shop-name table, data/shop_names.cfg, with patterns per trade: 'ห้างทอง{มงคล}' for gold, 'เจ๊{ชื่อ} {trade}' for food, '{ชื่อ}พานิช' for wholesale, 'คลินิกหมอ{ชื่อ}' for clinics, 'ร้านยา{ชื่อ}เภสัช' for pharmacies, and parody chains for the minimart. Pick with a hash of the building's origin cell, not the build RNG, so generation stays save-compatible with no GEN bump. (b) Draw green street-name blades at each junction listed in victory.cfg 'junctions' and blue 'ซอย N' signs at soi mouths, using the existing road names. (c) In city_map.gd, draw road names along roads and block names at block centres from the same cfg, plus 4-5 icons (monument, BTS station, hospital cross, market, mall), revealed with the explored area.

findings.title: The places a Thai player looks for at อนุสาวรีย์ชัย are missing, including a temple for the planned refugee camp
findings.observation: Fact: the canal (03) has a bare walkway on both banks with 2 vendor umbrellas, and a plain lawn north of it (00: the top strip y 0-40 is solid green). No temple, police box, petrol station or van-terminal crowd appears anywhere in the zone (00 blocks: military_hospital, hospital, shophouses, office, mall x2, market, shophouses). spawn=[191,176] (victory.cfg line 8) is the roundabout's south-west edge. ROADMAP 'ชั่วโมงแรก' makes a refugee camp in a temple the new-player spawn and the next agreed task, and phase 3 lists ตลาดสด, ปั๊มน้ำมัน, สถานีตำรวจ and โรงเรียน.
findings.evidence: 03_canal, 00_zone_map, victory.cfg lines 8, 28, 39-48; ROADMAP 'ชั่วโมงแรก', 'เฟส 3'
findings.why: Opinion: recognisability comes from 3-4 signature spots, not an exact footprint. For this district those are the boat-noodle shops along Khlong Sam Sen, the vans and buses around the ring, the police boxes, and vendors under the skywalk. Each is also a gameplay magnet: food, a crowd-turned-horde, and a later gun hint. The temple is needed anyway for the next milestone.
findings.suggestion: In victory.cfg: (1) add a thin shophouse block along the south bank of the canal next to Phahon Yothin with "use": "boat_noodle". Add a prefab data/prefabs/boat_noodle.txt with a boat-shaped counter, stacks of tiny bowls and low stools spilling onto the bank. (2) Add 2-4 police boxes (a 3x3 prefab) at the roundabout corners; for now they can hold only cues such as a rack, radio and papers, with guns later. (3) Reserve a walled temple lot (not a royal temple, parody name), for example 40x35 cells cut from the south-west shophouse block near ถนนโยธี, as "use": "temple_camp", and move spawn there when the camp lands. (4) Mark a 'van_terminal' strip on the Phaya Thai side of the ring and feed it to the L2 jam. Bump GEN.

findings.title: Tall-roof ghosts cover large parts of the screen and hide what stands under them
findings.observation: Fact: in 03_canal a translucent grey box spans x110-1280, y295-690, about 55% of the frame. It covers the canal, the bank and the player, and nothing says what it is; it is presumably the projected roof of the first military-hospital building, which starts at y 24. In 06_office a similar ghost box sits at x375-1010, y555-720. In 11_play_zoom the faded brown roof tints the pavement, and a tree canopy shows through two layers (tree, then roof), so depth is hard to read. Neighbouring roofs that are not faded (grey and beige in 11) fully hide the pavement strip in front of them.
findings.why: Opinion: at a glance the player must tell walkable ground from building and see who stands on it. A big murky rectangle reads as fog or a bug. A zombie standing on the pavement under an unfaded neighbouring roof is invisible, which will feel unfair in a game about sight lines.
findings.suggestion: In building_prop.gd's fade: when the player is inside a roof's projected area, fade to about 10-15% and draw a crisp 1-2 px roof outline plus the eave line, so it reads as 'a building above you'. Fade the whole footprint of big buildings, not partly. For any character (zombie or player) standing inside another building's roof projection, draw a flat silhouette over the roof (a people-only overlay, which fits the 'only people fade' rule and adds no area shade), only when the player's sight rays would reach that spot.

findings.title: The big compounds look alike, and their grounds read as noise with no paths
findings.observation: Fact: on 00 the military-hospital block (north-west) and the office/condo block (north-east) are each an even grid of about 16-19 similar grey rectangles on grass. In 04/20 (military hospital) and 06 (office) the building uses the same plan: rooms on both sides of an east-west corridor, stairs at both ends, left/right mirrored rooms. Both have the same flat beige roofs with AC units and the same parked sedans. The lawns in 05, 06 and 07 are sprinkled with pale concrete cells in a checkerboard-like scatter (05 lower half) and have no footpath to any entrance. The lot north of the market (08, y0-290) is about 30x10 m of concrete holding 1 car and 2 bins.
findings.why: Opinion: if the army hospital and the office park look the same from outside, the danger ladder planned in the roadmap (shophouse < mall/market < hospital < military) cannot be read on the ground. Paths and parking bays are how a top-down player finds the entrance without trying every wall.
findings.suggestion: Give each 'use' in big_plans.gd an exterior kit and 2-3 footprint options, driven by a per-use table. military_hospital: gatehouse, flagpole, parade ground, army trucks, sandbag rings (ties to L3). hospital: emergency drop-off canopy with ambulances, red-cross signs and ramps. office/condo: tower-on-podium or L-shape, guard booth, painted parking bays, rooftop billboard or pool. mall: big parody-name sign band and a taxi queue. For grounds: lay a paved path from each gate to each entrance, draw lawns as solid shapes with a kerb, and replace the scattered pale cells with either clean grass or a deliberate crack/weed pattern along paths. Fill empty lots with painted bays and cars, which gives cover and loot. Bump GEN.

findings.title: Shophouse rows all face south, leaving the main north-south roads without shop fronts
findings.observation: Fact: in 00 every shophouse row in both shophouse blocks runs east-west with its front facing south, broken into short clusters. Along Ratchaprarop (15) the east side shows roofs and the ร้านทอง facade at right angles to the road (x817-1170, y285-435). The west side is the market's roof. No entrance faces the 4-lane road. In 10 the pink ขายส่ง unit stands alone with empty concrete gaps of about 3 and 5 cells on either side (x190-310 and x630-830). Each soi has fronts on one side and blank backs on the other (09, 10).
findings.why: Opinion: real Bangkok main roads and sois are lined by continuous rows of 8-20 shophouses facing the street, fronts facing fronts across the soi. Detached 1-3 unit clusters with gaps read as suburban, and Ratchaprarop, Phaya Thai and Soi Rang Nam feel like service roads. Cost: in this 3/4 view a north-, east- or west-facing front is hidden or edge-on. That is presumably why everything faces south, and the fix below works around it rather than adding a camera angle.
findings.suggestion: (1) Cheap step: build longer continuous rows (6-12 units, party walls already exist) with a side soi every 40-60 cells. Narrow the back gaps to a 1-2 cell drainage alley with water jars, AC compressors and laundry. (2) Rows along north-south roads: allow east/west-facing prefabs (rotate the text prefab in city_gen.gd). Mark their fronts with things visible from above: Thai-style projecting blade signs drawn as south-facing boards sticking out over the pavement, an awning strip on the pavement side, and goods, tables and motorbikes spilling out. Real shophouses really do use perpendicular signs. (3) North-facing rows along a soi can be marked the same way, giving two-sided sois. Bump GEN.

findings.title: Big-building interiors lack identity: the market reads as an office and the mall has no shopfronts
findings.observation: Fact: the Soi Rang Nam market interior (08) is rows of brown desks topped with green-lit boxes and stacks of white-and-blue paper inside a walled hall. At a glance it reads as an open-plan office. The mall (07) has a concourse with a row of 8 identical wooden doors, each with a blue bench (x720-760, y0-470). A hair salon (red chairs and mirrors, around (1215,130-215)) and clothing (mannequins) sit in plain walled rooms with no shopfront or sign. The military-hospital ground floor (20) has 8 large rooms, each about 80% empty floor, with items only along the walls. By contrast, the market's street edge in 15 (bottom-left, coloured basins under an awning) does read as a market.
findings.why: Opinion: 'the salon on the ground floor of the mall' and 'the fish stalls at the back of the market' are how players remember and describe big buildings. Rooms that are mostly empty floor also make the big, risky buildings feel less rewarding than a shophouse.
findings.suggestion: Market: add a stall kit (furniture_prop.gd + items.cfg places). Low tables with pink/blue checked plastic sheeting, กะละมัง basins of produce, white styrofoam ice boxes with fish, hanging scales and bare bulbs, crates, rubber boots, stalls in irregular clusters. Make the hall open-sided with a translucent corrugated roof, and spill 3-6 stalls onto Soi Rang Nam. Mall: give each unit's south wall the shophouse facade treatment already in building_prop.gd (glass front, sign band with a parody brand, shutter). Hospital ground floor: add a reception counter, rows of waiting chairs and a pharmacy counter, and raise furniture density so rooms are at most about 50% empty. Bump GEN where layouts change.

findings.title: The skywalk ring and BTS are scenery with no visible way up and no supports
findings.observation: Fact: in 16_wide the skywalk ring (about 740 px across at zoom 1) circles the roundabout, but I could find no stair landing or ramp. At most there are small segment joints (for example near (985,330)). In 02 the BTS viaduct is a translucent band (x545-670) over the median with no piers on the ground. ROADMAP phase 5 lists 'เดินบนราง BTS'. The storey system (stairs per storey, zombies following storey by storey) already exists.
findings.evidence: 16_wide, 01_monument, 02_phahon_bts, 07_mall (top-left); ROADMAP 'เฟส 5', 'แกนกลาง รอบ 3'
findings.why: Opinion: the skywalk is the most recognisable part of this junction, and to a player it is an obvious escape route: get above the crowd, cross the ring, come down elsewhere. Showing it with no stairs invites the player to try and then get frustrated. Without piers the BTS band reads as a floating texture rather than a structure you are under.
findings.suggestion: Step 1 (S): draw 4-6 stair landings on the ring at the pavement corners, and BTS piers every 20-25 cells on the median (solid tiles, which needs a GEN bump). If the skywalk is not walkable yet, put a visible shutter, chain or barricade on each stair so it clearly reads as 'blocked for now'. Step 2 (L): make the skywalk storey 1 using the existing storey code. Stairs are the only way up, zombies climb slowly, and it gives the ring vendors and a stalled BTS train on the curve (a roadmap event) a place to be seen from.

findings.title: Roofs are the most-seen surface in the game, and most are bare
findings.observation: Fact: at zoom 2-2.5 roofs fill roughly 50-60% of 09, 10, 15, 17 and 18. The minimart roof in 18 (x240-520, y30-550) is flat grey with one bunting line, 2 AC units and a small box. The large corrugated roofs in 09 (x830-1070) and 15 (x975-1170) are single untextured sheets. A few blue or grey tanks appear (09 at (60,185) and (360,220)).
findings.why: Opinion: with a camera looking down, roof detail pays off more than anything else, and Bangkok rooftops are distinctive: stainless water tanks on stands, lean-to add-on rooms, laundry lines, potted herbs, satellite dishes, TV antennas, cage extensions, billboard frames facing the big roads. Roofs also matter in play: tanks (rain system), escape routes and future home claims.
findings.suggestion: Add a roof-prop table (for example data/roof_props.cfg): prop, weight per roof material and building use, max count per unit. Include a stainless tank on legs (tie it to the building's existing rooftop tank state, so the tank you see is the tank you use), a blue plastic tank, an add-on shack with corrugated roof, a laundry line, pots, a dish, an antenna, and a billboard frame (only on units facing a named main road; parody ads). Vary the material mix (flat concrete, tile, corrugated) with visible seams every unit so party walls read from above. New draws at the end of build, bump GEN.

findings.title: Night windows should mean something
findings.observation: Fact: in 13_night_street five shophouse front windows glow warm yellow (around (370,635), (180,695), (370,695), (855,695), (1275,695)) in a district where power is presumably out. ROADMAP round 4 says room lights at night only turn on in buildings powered by a generator. I cannot tell from the screenshot whether these windows follow that rule or are decorative.
findings.why: Opinion: after the outbreak a lit window is a strong signal: someone is there, or there is power. If decorative, it teaches players to ignore the best landmark a dark city has. If it follows generator power and player homes, it becomes a co-op beacon ('the lit house on Yothi is ours') and a lure for zombies and strangers.
findings.suggestion: Light facade windows only for buildings whose state has power or an active home (the same flag that lights interior bulbs), and optionally one rare 'mystery light' per zone from the planned events table. Draw the glow slightly onto the pavement so it reads from zoom 1-2.

verdicts.fact_check: main.gd:131 sets play_zoom to 4. project.godot:23-26 uses a 1280x720 base with stretch canvas_items/expand, so the view is 320x180 px = 20x11.25 cells and the player stands 5.6 m from the top and bottom edges. A runner moves 64 px/s (zombie.gd:10), so that edge distance is about 1.4 s of approach. 11_play_zoom matches, except that x385-577 is a soi mouth with lamp posts, not roof. Zoom is only on Ctrl+wheel (main.gd:1586-1590; the plain wheel changes the hotbar slot). play_zoom is never saved, so it resets to 4 on every launch. Context zoom already exists: on a roof the camera pulls back to 0.78x (main.gd:1199). On foot the aim lead is only ~22 px (main.gd:109, 1036). The analyst's 'fix the visible world size across monitors' is already done by the stretch mode. Costs the analyst missed: zombies spawn at 320 px or more (survival.gd:465), horde zombies at 280-420 px (survival.gd:396), and net.gd:221 keeps ZOMBIE_NEAR = 320 px 'at the usual zoom'. At zoom 2.5 the half-diagonal is 294 px, so horde zombies can pop in at the frame corners. At zoom 3 (half-extent 213x120) spawns stay off screen.
verdicts.reason: The framing problem is real and cheap to try. The resolution half is already solved, and zoom 2.5 collides with the spawn radii. Zoom 3 is the safe step. The wardrobe characters get 25% smaller at 3, so the user should compare 3 and 4 side by side before deciding.
verdicts.revised_observation: Zoom 4 shows 20x11 m, 5.6 m (~1.4 s of a runner) to the top and bottom edges. Zoom resets to 4 every launch and is hidden on Ctrl+wheel. Resolution independence already exists (canvas_items stretch).
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) Default play_zoom 3.0 (main.gd:131): about 27x15 m. (2) Save play_zoom in the settings cfg. (3) Teach Ctrl+wheel in the tutorial and the Esc help. (4) Optional: extend the roof_k blend at main.gd:1199 with an inside factor (hidden_building != null gives x1.25) so interiors stay near 4. Stay at 2.8 or above unless the spawn radius (survival.gd:396, 465) and ZOMBIE_NEAR are raised. Check F3/?bench, and A/B 3 vs 4 in one play session.

verdicts.fact_check: Traffic comes from city_gen.gd:915-922: each road gets length/7 tries, with the lane picked from {0,1,wd-2,wd-1}, so cars sit only in the kerb lanes. _vehicle refuses any cell next to another blocked cell (972-975), so nose-to-tail queues are impossible. The roundabout is drawn with _disk (202-205) and is not in w.roads, so the ring gets no traffic and no wrecks by construction. Pile-ups happen only at the 3 junctions in victory.cfg:22 (999-1010). In 01 and 16 the ring is empty; the sedan and van in 01 are on the radial roads. Already present: bus stops on all four arms and a 5-van stand west of the ring (city_gen.gd:303-324), plus wrecks every 22 cells (1012-1019). Trunk search is planned (ROADMAP เฟส 2 'ค้นท้ายรถ'). Every vehicle is already climbable (street_prop.gd:12).
verdicts.reason: The observation is right and the most important empty space is the ring itself. The GEN bump is unnecessary: new street props appended last, with their own RNG, do not touch the test_city fingerprint (tests/test_city.gd:11-24 hashes tiles/doors/containers/buildings only). Impact rises to 5 once trunk search exists.
verdicts.revised_observation: By construction the ring road has zero vehicles. The avenues get only kerb-lane parked cars, and the gap rule forbids any queue. The bus stops and van stand already exist.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Add _jam(w), called last in CityGen.build after _landmarks, with its own RNG seeded from w.city_seed + const, the way _landmarks does (city_gen.gd:316-318). Read optional 'jam' (0-1) and 'toward' per road, and 'jam' on the circle, from victory.cfg. Fill the inner lanes nose-to-tail, bypassing the gap rule but keeping one full lane plus the kerb lane open, and nothing in junctions or in front of doors. On the ring, place vehicles along arcs rotated to the tangent. Append motorbikes after everything else so bike ids (vehicles.gd:60-70) stay stable. No GEN bump; test_city's reachability check will catch walled-in doors. Start with Phahon Yothin and the ring at 0.7 and Ratchawithi at 0.3, and measure at zoom 1 over the ring.

verdicts.fact_check: The analyst missed the existing aftermath layer. _aftermath (city_gen.gd:995-1075) places pile-ups, wrecks, papers, luggage, drag marks and dropped bags. _checkpoint (1141-1166) puts sandbags, a barrier and an army truck at one random junction at least 400 px from spawn; in this zone that is one of 3 junctions, never at the hospital or the monument. Facades carry spray messages 35% of the time (GRAFFITI includes 'หนีไปวัด', 'อย่าเข้า' and 'ไม่มีของแล้ว'; building_prop.gd:34, 416-420) plus rescue X-codes (421-430). Roofs get SOS signs and tarp shelters (243-257). ROADMAP marks 'เมืองรอบ 1: ซากหลังหายนะ (รถชน ด่านทหาร ของตกหล่น)' as done. The screenshots do confirm that the hospital grounds and the monument island are clean (04, 20, 01, 16).
verdicts.reason: Traces exist but are scattered at random. The real gap is authored placement at story sites. Most scenes can reuse props that already exist, and adding props only needs no GEN bump.
verdicts.revised_observation: Aftermath props, graffiti and one army checkpoint exist but are placed at random. The hospital gates, the monument plaza and the bus stops tell no story, and the checkpoint lands on an arbitrary junction.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Step 1 (S): add an optional 'checkpoint': [x,y,w,h] to victory.cfg, for example the military hospital gate on Ratchawithi. Keep the existing rng draw in _checkpoint and only override the chosen rect, so the random stream is unchanged. Step 2 (M): add 'scenes': [{kind, at}] to victory.cfg, placed by _scenes(w), called last with its own RNG. Compose scenes first from existing props (sandbags, barrier, army truck, luggage, papers, drag, bus/van, glass), then add 2-3 new drawings in street_prop.gd (tent, cot, stretcher). First three: a failed evacuation at the monument bus stops (buses with open doors, luggage), triage at the hospital front, the checkpoint at the army hospital gate.

verdicts.fact_check: The 'searched looks different' part is already built. furniture_prop.gd:4 says 'Looks emptier once searched': shelves show 1 item instead of 4 (line 57), doors hang open (118-119), glass turns dull (88, 141) and stall goods disappear (240). The screenshots just show unsearched furniture. Loot is rolled at search time (inventory.gd:596 calling Items.roll) with a flat empty chance per furniture kind (EMPTY: fridge 0.3, stall 0.35, default 0.15; items.gd:655-680). Nothing varies by building. ROADMAP หาความสนุก names 'ของมีทุกบ้าน' as a reason players never take risks.
verdicts.reason: The core idea (picked-over buildings) is new, fits the roadmap's fun diagnosis, and needs no generation change because loot is rolled at search time. The analyst's second half is already done, and the GEN bump is unnecessary.
verdicts.revised_observation: Every building starts equally stocked (a flat empty chance per furniture kind). Searched containers already look emptier; there is no 'picked over before you arrived' state.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: In inventory.gd, before Items.roll, scale the empty chance by a building factor from World.hash01(building seed, ...). Keep the numbers in a small table (items.gd or items.cfg), for example pharmacy/minimart/clinic 0.5-0.7, gold shop 0.8, homes deep in sois 0.1, big buildings 0.2 (their shut-in zombies kept looters out). Draw the same hash as a ransacked look: litter decals, a toppled shelf, a shutter forced half up. No GEN bump. Leave barricaded homes for the spray-paint home claiming.

verdicts.fact_check: Road names are stored (city_gen.gd:190) but never drawn anywhere. Only the hospital and market block names reach signs (700-707), and offices and malls use SIGN_NAMES (641-645). There are 18 trades, not 11 (SIGNS, city_gen.gd:30-32), and 25% of shops have no sign (379). 00 is only the raw tile picture. The real M map (city_map.gd:199-247) does show the zone name, 'ไป…' exit labels, pins and a legend, but no road or block labels and no landmark icons. Its legend is wrong for this zone: it lists วัด and คอนโด, which don't exist here, while hospitals, malls, the market and offices all share one brown (6e665a; city_map.gd:38-41, 239-240). A green text-board prop already exists for zone exits (city_gen.gd:1215-1218).
verdicts.reason: The claim is right with small corrections, and it is highly actionable because the names already exist in the data. Street signs and map labels are cheap and need no GEN bump; shop names can be derived from the seed at render time.
verdicts.revised_observation: Road and block names exist in victory.cfg but are never shown in the world or on the map. The map legend is stale for this zone, and big buildings are indistinguishable on the map.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) S: a 'streetsign' prop reusing the zonesign drawing, at both ends of every named road and at each junction, placed last. (2) S-M: in city_map.gd, draw w.roads names along each road and w.blocks names at block centres, add icons for the monument (w.circle) and the BTS path and station, colour big buildings by kind, and build the legend from what the zone actually contains. (3) M: a shop-name table in data (patterns per trade, parody chains for minimarts), picked in BuildingProp from data.seed at render time. Keep the trade word so shops still read by what they sell.

verdicts.fact_check: Correct that the zone has no temple, police box or petrol station (victory.cfg:39-48). Wrong that there is no van terminal: _landmarks places bus stops and a 5-van stand (city_gen.gd:303-324; ROADMAP ✅ 'ป้ายรถเมล์ ท่ารถตู้เก่า'). spawn [191,176] is correct. The temple camp is the next agreed step (ROADMAP ชั่วโมงแรก, ลำดับ 3; skills and quests are done). _temple_block exists (city_gen.gd:829-845), but _layout_plan only routes BLOCK_USES or shophouses (217-220). Facades already carry the graffiti 'หนีไปวัด' (building_prop.gd:34), pointing to a temple that doesn't exist. Rows 0-13 north of Khlong Sam Sen are bare lawn across the whole zone (00 top band, 03 top half); no block covers them.
verdicts.reason: Timely because of the camp. The analyst's canal-side block would eat into the hospital compound, but the empty lawn north of the canal is free, and a row there would face south onto the towpath, the side the 3/4 view shows.
verdicts.revised_observation: No temple (needed next for the camp), police box or petrol station. The bus stops and van stand exist. Rows 0-13 north of the canal are empty lawn across the zone.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) S code + data: route 'use': 'temple' in _layout_plan to _temple_block. Reserve a ~40x35 lot, for example the west end of the SW shophouse block near ถนนโยธี. Non-royal, parody name. Spawn moves there with the camp. (2) Data: add blocks [0,0,191,14] and [209,0,191,14] as shophouses, giving one south-facing row on the north towpath, plus an optional per-block 'signs' bias (e.g. 50% ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือ, which already has its own stall drawing). (3) Later: police boxes as a 3x3 prefab at two ring corners, cues only until guns arrive (phase 3). GEN bump for (1) and (2).

verdicts.fact_check: _fade_trees_near (main.gd:1296-1318) fades whole building nodes to alpha 0.3, but only when their visual rect overlaps the player's body (or, when inside, the tall buildings south of it). Trees fade to 0.45, the BTS and skywalk to 0.45. So the whole footprint already fades. 03: the ghost box carries rooftop tanks; it is the faded roof of the military hospital. 06: the same. 11: the unfaded grey and beige roofs hide the pavement north of them. Characters y-sort behind buildings, so a zombie on a pavement behind an unfaded row is invisible even when Sight says the character sees it (main.gd:1175-1185).
verdicts.reason: The hidden-zombie problem is real and matters for fairness. The per-character silhouette adds a draw per zombie, and zombies are the known cost. Reusing the existing fade is cheaper.
verdicts.revised_observation: Only the building directly in front of the player fades (to 0.3, whole node). A seen zombie behind any other roof stays hidden.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: S: in _fade_trees_near, also fade any building whose visual_rect covers a zombie or player with sight_k > 0.5 within ~250 px, capped to the 2 nearest. Then try building alpha 0.2 plus a 1 px roof outline drawn when faded, and compare in the 03/11 spots. Keep per-character silhouettes as the fallback only if this looks too murky.

verdicts.fact_check: 00 shows about 16 buildings in the NW block and 19 in the NE block. BLOCK_USES (city_gen.gd:634-640) cycles [hospital, flats, hospital, office] and [office, flats]. All of these kinds use the same corridor plan (big_plans.gd:7-9, 54-116). The lawn checkerboard comes from city_gen.gd:684-685: only 85% of clear cells become grass or tree, and the other 15% stay concrete (SOI) at random. The military hospital differs only by its wall (720-734). Car parks get ordinary cars (708-717). BigPlans are rectangles only (roadmap: 'ตึกต้องเป็นสี่เหลี่ยม'), so L-shapes or a tower on a podium would be a big job.
verdicts.reason: The observation holds, and the checkerboard has a one-line cause. The analyst's footprint variety is L; distinct exteriors can come from props that already exist.
verdicts.revised_observation: The two compounds hold about 35 corridor buildings with the same plan. The lawn speckle comes from a random 15% concrete holdover (city_gen.gd:684-685).
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) S: fill all clear lawn cells (drop the 0.85 roll). (2) S: give the military hospital its identity from existing props: 'army' trucks instead of cars in its car parks (street_prop.gd:25, 56-85), the checkpoint at its gate (L3), a flagpole. (3) S-M: wider spacing and one open parade ground for military_hospital in _big_block. (4) Later: an ambulance bay at hospital fronts and painted parking bays. Skip new footprints. GEN bump.

verdicts.fact_check: 00 and 10 confirm the short clusters. The cause: _shophouse_block cuts a full-height cross-soi every 12-16 cells (city_gen.gd:763-767, SOI_W 3), so each row segment holds only 1-2 units (SHOP_W 6-7). On top of that there is a 7% chance of a 2-cell walkway (808-811). These are the 3- and 5-cell gaps in 10. All fronts face south by design: BuildingProp draws only a south facade (building_prop.gd:3-5). An east-, west- or north-facing front is a face this camera never shows, so rotated prefabs amount to a new view, which the scope rule forbids, and they would mean rewriting prefabs, doors, shutters and stairs.
verdicts.reason: The cheap fix is a one-number change with big realism payoff. The rotation half should be dropped, and the narrower-back-alley idea breaks the soi the fronts face.
verdicts.revised_observation: Rows are 1-2 units long because a cross-soi is cut every 12-16 cells. The south-only fronts are a projection constraint.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: (1) S: change the cross-soi step at city_gen.gd:767 to about 36 + randi_range(0, 24). That gives rows of 5-9 units and a soi every 40-60 m. Keep the 7% walkway. GEN bump + fingerprint. (2) Drawing only: the end unit beside a north-south road (Ratchaprarop) gets a side blade sign and an awning on its road-side wall. Drop rotated prefabs and the narrower back alleys. See missed M1 for fronts on the main roads.

verdicts.fact_check: _market (big_plans.gd:408-433) fills the stall rows with 'k' counters 45%, 't' tables 25%, then sacks, boxes and pots. These are the same counters shophouses use, set in back-to-back rows, so 08 reads as desks. A 'stall' furniture (letter H) already exists, but it is the eatery's food cart (furniture_prop.gd:235-280). 20 shows sparse rooms. 07 shows salon chairs and mannequins in walled units behind plain doors.
verdicts.reason: Accurate and specific. The market is the best identity-per-effort gain; the mall shopfronts can come last.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: Market first: add a 'marketstall' furniture (a new letter in PLAN_FURNITURE, city_gen.gd:60-61; a draw in furniture_prop.gd modelled on _draw_stall: checked cloth, basins, ice box; a FURN_LOOT entry) and use it for the 'k' share in _market. Vary goods by the table each row already gets (big_plans.gd:421). Then raise hospital ground-floor density in _furnish. Mall shopfronts last. GEN bump.

verdicts.fact_check: The pillar claim is wrong. Pillars stand every 10 cells along the BTS path on road, pavement or plaza (city_gen.gd:265-279) and are drawn as columns with caps (street_prop.gd:418-424). In 02 they show faintly on the median at about (605,150-185) and (605,440-500), under a deck faded to 0.45 because the player stands beneath it (main.gd:1320-1326). The station has stairs down to both pavements (city_gen.gd:280-290). The skywalk ring really has no stairs and no supports (overhead.gd:122-140, and no street prop for it); 16 confirms. Walking on the BTS is planned for phase 5.
verdicts.reason: Half the observation is wrong. The skywalk stairs are a cheap, prop-only fix; making it walkable stays in phase 5.
verdicts.revised_observation: The skywalk ring has no stairs or supports. BTS pillars exist but read weakly under the faded deck.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: S: add 'skywalkstairs' props (reusing the _bts_stairs drawing) where the ring crosses the four corner pavements, and 'pillar' props about every 10 cells round the ring, placed last. No tile change, no GEN bump. Pressing E on the stairs says the way up is closed for now. The walkable skywalk via storeys comes later with phase 5.

verdicts.fact_check: Most of the suggested props already exist in building_prop.gd:160-258: corrugated roofs 35% of the time (striped, with rust spots) or 6 concrete/painted tones, stains, 1-3 AC units, a laundry line 40%, pots 30%, a tank 70%, an antenna 40%, moss, a stainless tank on legs 30%, a satellite dish 25%, a solar heater 12%, a tyre and planks, and SOS/tarp/ช่วยด้วย. Roofs look bare because shophouse roofs are 13-15 cells deep (208-240 px) while each prop is 5-15 px and appears at most once per roof. In 18, a roof of about 280x520 px holds 2 AC units and a box. Roofs are drawn at render time from data.seed, not by CityGen, so no GEN bump applies.
verdicts.reason: The list is mostly already built. The real issue is density against roof size, and roofs fill half the screen.

Add the missing Thai element: a corrugated add-on room or lean-to over the back third of shophouse roofs, around the stair hut. Add billboard frames only on roofs next to named roads. verdicts.fact_check: To settle the analyst's doubt: the windows are decorative. building_prop.gd:790-808 lights shophouse windows 30% of the time by seed, minimart fronts always, and condo windows 18%, all with no power check. Only big buildings check data.lit (776-778). data.lit is set for every building by World.set_powered (world.gd:454-467), and World.is_lit (489-500), which stealth uses, treats an unpowered room as dark. So a glowing window lies to the player. ROADMAP รอบ 4 says bulbs light only in powered buildings.
verdicts.reason: A verified inconsistency with a one-line fix, and it turns lit windows into the co-op beacon the analyst describes.
verdicts.revised_observation: Shophouse, minimart and condo windows glow by seed with no power check; big buildings obey power. The stealth lighting treats those same rooms as dark.
verdicts.revised_suggestion: At the top of _draw_glow, return unless data.get('lit') or the title screen's all_lit (world.gd:452). Later, when the planned 'week 1 grid still on' rule lands (หาความสนุก, โลกเปลี่ยนตามวัน), light a share of windows by day count. Optional: a glow spill onto the pavement below lit facades.

missed.title: Not one shop front faces a named road: every main road is lined by compounds, backs of rows or side walls
missed.observation: Every shophouse faces south, and _shophouse_block packs rows from the block's top edge, leaving any remainder as a vacant lot at the bottom (city_gen.gd:776-796). In victory.cfg both shophouse blocks lie SOUTH of their roads (Ratchawithi and ถนนโยธี), so those roads see only row backs and roofs. North of the east-west roads there are only the hospital and office compounds. Result: none of the 8 named road segments has a shophouse front. 11: ถนนโยธี shows backs and roofs. 12: Ratchawithi shows hospital grounds and a wall. 15: Ratchaprarop shows side walls and the market roof. 02: Phahon Yothin shows grounds and an office. Even the south map-edge pavement is cut off by a vacant-lot strip (00: green squares along the bottom of the SE block).
missed.why: In this 3/4 view the only facade you can see is a south-facing one. So shopfronts along a road can only come from rows on the NORTH side of an east-west road, and the zone plan has none. Main-road shop frontage is the most Bangkok image there is, and it is where loot-and-risk decisions should happen. Today the main roads are the dullest spaces in the zone, which is part of why L2 and L6 feel empty.
missed.suggestion: Zone data first: carve a 15-row shophouse strip along the north side of Ratchawithi east (for example [224,136,176,15], taken from the office block) so its fronts face Ratchawithi across the pavement; optionally do the same west of the roundabout. In _shophouse_block, when the block's south edge meets a named road's pavement, pack rows from the bottom, so the last row fronts the pavement and the leftover lot goes to the top. Pair this with M2 so these frontages hold pharmacies, gold shops and minimarts. GEN bump + fingerprint.

missed.title: Trades and minimarts ignore location, so loot geography is flat

Loot follows the trade (SIGN_LOOT city_gen.gd:42-50; rec.table at 475), so food, water and medicine are equally close in every soi.

missed.why: Real Bangkok puts pharmacies, gold shops, clinics and 7-Elevens on main roads and at soi mouths, with homes, eateries and repair shops deeper in. That same geography is the risk/reward map the core loop needs: the good stuff sits on the loud, open main road, while the quiet soi is safer but poorer. It answers the roadmap's own diagnosis that nothing is worth a risk.
missed.suggestion: Add a small table (in victory.cfg or data/trades.cfg) of trade weights by frontage class: 'main' (front on a named road's pavement, or the first unit at a soi mouth), 'soi', and 'market' (within N cells of a market block). For example, main: pharmacy 3, gold 2, clinic 2, phone 2, minimart 2, eateries 1; soi: unsigned home 4, eateries 3, repair 2, barber 1, minimart 0.3. In add_building, classify by the tile in front of the front door and pick from the table instead of uniformly from SIGNS. Cap minimarts at about 1 per 60 cells of frontage. GEN bump.
